steps/8.description: Because the autopod developmental program is reused in the hands and feet, disrupted IHH or GDF5-BMPR1B signaling produces shortening or absence of homologous phalangeal segments across both sets of digits. evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists short hallux as a very frequent feature of brachydactyly type A1, reflecting the foot involvement mirroring the thumb changes.

steps/15.description: Shortening of the great toe (hallux) proximal phalanx occurs in BDA1 in parallel to the thumb involvement of the hands.

evidence.snippet: HP:0010579 | Cone-shaped epiphysis | Frequent (79-30%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists cone-shaped epiphysis as a frequent radiographic feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/16.description: Cone-shaped epiphyses of the middle phalanges are a characteristic radiographic finding in BDA1, arising from the abnormal endochondral ossification due to impaired IHH-Patched1 signaling.

evidence.snippet: HP:0001204 | Distal symphalangism (hands) | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists distal symphalangism of hands as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/17.description: Fusion of the distal interphalangeal joints (symphalangism) is an occasional finding in BDA1, reflecting the variable extent of phalanx fusion seen in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: HP:0004209 | Clinodactyly of the 5th finger | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists clinodactyly of the 5th finger as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/18.description: Lateral deviation of the fifth finger (clinodactyly) is an occasional digital feature in BDA1, secondary to asymmetric shortening of the middle phalanx.

evidence.snippet: HP:0001230 | Broad metacarpals | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists broad metacarpals as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/19.description: Broadening of the metacarpals is an occasional skeletal feature recorded in the Orphanet phenotype profile for BDA1.

evidence.snippet: HP:0001762 | Talipes equinovarus | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists talipes equinovarus as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/20.description: Talipes equinovarus is an occasional lower-limb skeletal feature recorded for BDA1 in Orphanet.

evidence.snippet: HP:0002650 | Scoliosis | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists scoliosis as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/21.description: Scoliosis is an occasional axial skeletal feature recorded for BDA1 in Orphanet.

evidence.snippet: HP:0003022 | Hypoplasia of the ulna | Occasional (29-5%)
evidence.explanation: Orphanet lists hypoplasia of the ulna as an occasional feature of brachydactyly type A1.

steps/22.description: Ulnar hypoplasia is an occasional upper-limb feature recorded for BDA1 in Orphanet.

evidence.snippet: all three mutations affected Hh binding to the receptor Patched1 (PTC1), reducing its capacity to induce cellular differentiation
evidence.explanation: Functional assays connect defective IHH-Patched1 binding to reduced cellular differentiation.

edges/5.description: Reduced receptor binding and signaling capacity impair the IHH-dependent differentiation program that patterns phalangeal segments.

evidence.snippet: The combination of these features alters signaling capacity and range, but the impact is likely to be variable and mutation-dependent.
evidence.explanation: The experimental study links altered IHH stability, fate, and extracellular interactions to reduced signaling capacity and range.

edges/6.description: Instability, intracellular degradation, and altered extracellular interactions reduce the effective range of IHH signaling during digit development.

evidence.snippet: GDF5 interacts directly as the preferred ligand for the BMP type-1 receptor BMPR1B and is important for both chondrogenesis and digit formation.
evidence.explanation: The study identifies the ligand-receptor relationship and the shared developmental processes connecting GDF5-BMPR1B dysfunction to BDA1.

edges/7.description: Reduced GDF5 ligand activity or BMPR1B receptor activity impairs chondrogenesis and digit formation upstream of phalangeal segment specification.

evidence.snippet: In BDA1, a high concentration of IHH suppresses apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Connects the BDA1 IHH lesion to failure of interzone apoptosis.

edges/8.description: Deregulated IHH levels in the developing interzone block the apoptosis that normally drives joint cavitation.

evidence.snippet: Brachydactyly type A1 is a limb malformation characterized by a uniform shortening of the middle phalanges in all digits.
evidence.explanation: Uniform involvement across all digits documents the serially homologous hand-and-foot output of the developmental lesion.

edges/9.description: The same disrupted segment-specification program operates in fore- and hindlimb autopods, producing a coordinated hand-and-foot malformation rather than an isolated digit defect.

evidence.snippet: The proband, a 9-year-old boy, his siblings, and his father had shortened digits and a short stature of variable severity.
evidence.explanation: A molecularly confirmed family links the IHH-associated digit phenotype with variably expressed short stature.

edges/10.description: The growth-plate defect can extend beyond the digits and reduce linear skeletal growth, although expression is variable among families.

edges/11.description: Clubfoot is an occasional broader limb-development outcome; the intermediate steps beyond altered limb morphogenesis are unresolved.

edges/12.description: Scoliosis is an occasional broader skeletal association; its precise mechanistic connection to the digit-patterning lesion is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals show hypoplasia of the ulnar styloid processes, ulna minus, osteoarthritis, normal length of all distal phalanges and shortening or absence of the middle phalanges.
evidence.explanation: A molecularly confirmed IHH family documents proximal ulnar involvement together with the defining phalangeal phenotype.

edges/13.description: Ulnar hypoplasia extends the growth defect proximally within the upper limb, with incompletely defined intermediates.

evidence.snippet: a missing middle phalangeal bone is due to the failure of the developing joint to cavitate
evidence.explanation: Ties the cavitation failure directly to the missing skeletal element.

edges/14.description: Segments that fail to separate present as shortened or absent middle phalanges with symphalangism across the homologous digits.

evidence.snippet: Cavitation is the physical separation of the cartilage templates, and failure leads to joint fusions.
evidence.explanation: States the direct relationship between failed cavitation and joint fusion.

edges/15.description: An uncavitated interzone is, by definition, a fused joint.

evidence.snippet: three heterozygous missense mutations in the region encoding the amino-terminal signaling domain in all affected members of three large, unrelated families
evidence.explanation: Three independent families with distinct IHH missense mutations establish genotype-phenotype relationship.

evidence.snippet: The three mutant amino acids, which are conserved across all vertebrates and invertebrates studied so far, are predicted to be adjacent on the surface of IHH
evidence.explanation: Deep evolutionary conservation and surface clustering suggest a critical functional domain.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous missense mutations in the Indian Hedgehog (IHH) gene have been identified as a cause of BDA1
evidence.explanation: Confirms IHH missense mutations as the established cause of BDA1.

evidence.snippet: We report here on the first deletion in IHH, p.delE95, causing mild BrachydactylyA1 in a small Dutch family.
evidence.explanation: Expands the established pathogenic spectrum beyond missense variants to an in-frame IHH deletion.

evidence.snippet: Many are located in the C-terminal domain of IHH (IHH-C), which lacks signaling activity but is critical for auto-cleavage and activation of the N-terminal (IHH-N) peptide.
evidence.explanation: Extends the pathogenic territory beyond the N-terminal signalling domain to the C-terminal domain that processes it - relevant because IHH-C variants were previously being called variants of uncertain significance.

evidence.snippet: In vitro studies were performed for 9 IHH heterozygous variants, to test their effect on secretion and IHH intracellular processing by western blot of cells expressing each variant.
evidence.explanation: Describes the functional assay used to reclassify IHH variants of uncertain significance.

genes/0.notes: Heterozygous pathogenic IHH variants are the canonical cause of BDA1. Classic alleles are missense substitutions in the N-terminal signaling domain (including E95K, D100E, and E131K), but pathogenic in-frame deletions have also been demonstrated. Effects include altered stability, receptor binding, trafficking, and extracellular interactions.

evidence.snippet: Sequencing of the GDF5 coding region revealed that a mildly affected individual in the family was heterozygous, and that all of the severely affected individuals were homozygous for a novel missense c.1195C>T mutation that predicts a p.Arg399Cys substitution at a highly conserved amino acid.
evidence.explanation: Segregation in a consanguineous family demonstrates dosage-dependent GDF5-associated BDA1.

evidence.snippet: Functional analysis demonstrated that although the p.Arg399Cys mutant is able to stimulate chondrogenesis, it is much less effective than wild-type GDF5.
evidence.explanation: Functional assays show reduced chondrogenic activity of the BDA1-associated GDF5 allele.

evidence.snippet: The family was found to have an autosomal-dominantly inherited combination of BDA1 and SYNS2 caused by the S475N variant in the GDF5 gene.
evidence.explanation: A single GDF5 allele producing BDA1 together with multiple-synostoses syndrome 2, reinforcing that GDF5 phenotype depends on the allele rather than the gene.

genes/1.notes: Semidominant GDF5 variants can produce mild BDA1 in heterozygotes and a more severe phenotype in homozygotes. Reduced ligand activity impairs chondrogenesis upstream of IHH.

evidence.snippet: We report pathogenic variants in BMPR1B that are associated with complex BDA1.
evidence.explanation: The human genetic study identifies BMPR1B variants in individuals with complex BDA1.

evidence.snippet: Both mutations are most likely to act in a dominant-negative manner, similar to the effects observed in BMPR1B mutations that cause BDA2.
evidence.explanation: The authors interpret the two BDA1-associated BMPR1B variants as dominant-negative alleles.

genes/2.notes: Heterozygous missense and splice-site BMPR1B variants have been reported in complex BDA1 and are predicted to act through a dominant-negative mechanism, illustrating phenotypic continuity between BDA1 and BDA2.

evidence.snippet: The nature of genetic counseling depends both on the pattern of inheritance of the type of brachydactyly present in the family and on the presence or absence of accompanying symptoms.
evidence.explanation: The clinical review directly supports inheritance- and phenotype-specific counseling.

treatments/0.description: Genetic counseling for affected families given autosomal dominant inheritance and the historical significance of BDA1 as the first recorded Mendelian trait.

evidence.snippet: Physical therapy and ergotherapy may ameliorate hand function.
evidence.explanation: The management review supports function-directed rehabilitation.

treatments/1.description: Physical and occupational therapy may improve hand function when functional limitation is present.

evidence.snippet: Plastic surgery is only indicated if the brachydactyly affects hand function or for cosmetic reasons, but is typically not needed.
evidence.explanation: The review defines the limited indications for surgery.

treatments/2.description: Surgery is reserved for meaningful hand-function impairment or selected cosmetic indications and is usually unnecessary.

evidence.snippet: After treatment, the siblings' height improved significantly, and they acquired a significant increase in the height standard deviation score (SDS) (the boy: +2.54, the girl: +1.86) during the 4-year therapy. No noticeable adverse effect was observed during rhGH treatment.
evidence.explanation: Two siblings improved over four years, but uncontrolled case-level evidence limits generalization.

treatments/3.description: rhGH may be considered for clinically significant short stature in selected IHH-related cases; evidence is limited to a two-sibling case report and does not show correction of the hand malformation.

evidence.snippet: In this work, we have identified a cohort of 46 unrelated patients bearing de novo heterozygous germline missense mutations in H3F3A or H3F3B with a core phenotype of progressive neurologic dysfunction and congenital anomalies.
evidence.explanation: The founding cohort establishing de novo heterozygous missense variants as the cause.

evidence.snippet: Most of the causative variants are private and scattered throughout the protein, but all seem to have either a gain-of-function or dominant negative effect on protein function.
evidence.explanation: This review proposes gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects; it does not experimentally classify every allele.

steps/1.description: Heterozygous pathogenic H3-3A missense substitutions alter a core nucleosomal protein. Most are rare and distributed across the tail and core, but recurrent alleles occur. Dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanisms have been proposed; variant-specific biochemical effects include both increases and decreases in measured abundance or interactions. Haploinsufficiency is not established as the general explanation.

evidence.snippet: Molecular modeling of all 37 variants demonstrated clear disruptions in interactions with DNA, other histones, and histone chaperone proteins.
evidence.explanation: The structural modelling result this node records; evidence source is COMPUTATIONAL because the claim comes from in silico modelling.

evidence.snippet: Molecular modeling revealed that mutations in the histone core likely affect nucleosome stability, while the mutations in the tail affect various protein-protein interactions.
evidence.explanation: Gives the domain split between nucleosome destabilisation and disrupted protein-protein interaction.

steps/2.description: Structural modeling predicts changes at DNA contacts, inter-histone interfaces and chaperone-binding surfaces. Tail and core substitutions need not share one biochemical effect. Modeling does not prove universal nucleosome destabilization or demonstrate that every mutant is normally incorporated; those questions require allele-specific assays.

evidence.snippet: Three variant constructs (p.R129H, p.M121I, and p.I52N) showed significant decrease in protein expression, while one variant (p.R41C) accumulated at greater levels than wild-type control.
evidence.explanation: Transient HEK293T expression: R129H, M121I and R41C are H3-3A alleles; I52N is H3-3B and is not assigned to BLBS1.

steps/3.description: In transient HEK293T assays, H3-3A R129H and M121I reduce protein abundance whereas R41C increases it. The experiment measures steady-state expression and does not by itself distinguish altered synthesis from degradation or establish patient-neuronal dosage.

evidence.snippet: The Co-IP assays showed that p.R129H had a significantly stronger interaction with DAXX, suggesting that this variant might affect the deposition of histone H3.3
evidence.explanation: The interaction was measured; altered deposition was inferred. HGVS p.Arg129His corresponds to mature-histone R128H.

evidence.snippet: there was a complete loss of associations between H3.3 G90R and DAXX
evidence.explanation: Preprint BioID and immunoprecipitation identify loss of interaction for G90R; mature-histone G90R equals HGVS G91R.

steps/4.description: H3-3A R129H increases DAXX co-immunoprecipitation despite reduced histone abundance. Nuclear localization is preserved. Increased binding does not prove greater chromatin deposition. A newer preprint finds loss of DAXX association for mature-histone G90R, underscoring assay- and allele-dependent effects.

evidence.snippet: Patient histone posttranslational modifications (PTMs) analysis revealed notably aberrant local PTM patterns distinct from the somatic lysine mutations that cause global PTM dysregulation.
evidence.explanation: The abstract emphasizes local effects; full-text results also report modest global changes.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data suggest that the mutant histones can be incorporated into the nucleosome, cause marked local deregulation of chromatin state, and modestly alter the global control of histone modifications.
evidence.explanation: This conclusion explicitly includes modest global effects.

steps/5.description: Patient-derived lymphoblast and fibroblast assays identify prominent local modification changes on mutant histones, with more modest global changes. H3-3A A15G affects nearby K9/K14 modification; the reported A29P/K27/K36 example belongs to H3-3B. These observations support cis effects without proving that all downstream consequences are local or that all BLBS variants differ uniformly from somatic oncohistones.

evidence.snippet: H3.3 T45I stimulates the enzymatic activities of SETD2 and NSD1
evidence.explanation: Preprint biochemical nucleosome assays support increased activity toward the recurrent H3-3A T45I substrate; this does not establish a treatment target in patients.

evidence.snippet: increased H3.3K36me3 levels with S31F and T45I, and a complete to near complete loss of signal with G34V, K36E, and L48R
evidence.explanation: Preprint cell assays show opposite allele-specific effects. The H3-3A T45I finding is relevant here; the other substitutions are protein-level comparators, not all BLBS1 alleles.

steps/6.description: A 2025 preprint identifies increased H3K36 methylation in cis for H3.3 T45I and stimulation of SETD2/NSD1 activity on recombinant mutant nucleosomes. Other substitutions have opposite effects. Structural modeling implicates contacts with the methyltransferase AWS domain; that structural explanation remains a model.

evidence.snippet: the associations between PWWP and the S31 and T45I point mutants increased while those with G34V, K36E, and L48R generally decreased.
evidence.explanation: Preprint proximity data show directionally distinct effects among substitutions.

steps/7.description: Variant-dependent H3K36 modification alters association with PWWP-domain proteins, including DNMT3A/B. T45I increases selected reader associations in the preprint; this must not be replaced by a universal loss-of-DNMT3A claim derived from G34R. Consequences for DNA methylation and neuronal function require direct testing for individual H3-3A alleles.

evidence.snippet: RNA sequencing on patient cells demonstrated up-regulated gene expression related to mitosis and cell division, and cellular assays confirmed an increased proliferative capacity.
evidence.explanation: Provides both the transcriptional and the functional evidence for increased proliferation.

steps/8.description: RNA sequencing of three H3-3A patient fibroblast lines identified altered expression enriched for mitosis and cell division. Proliferation assays across five patient lines from both H3.3 genes found increased proliferative capacity. This is a non-neural cellular phenotype; neither a direct cause of neuronal dysfunction nor malignant transformation was demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: only H3-N108S shows significant trapping of the Spt16 subunit of yFACT at the 3’ end
evidence.explanation: Yeast native-H3 experiments identify a variant-specific defect. N108S is not assigned as a human H3-3A allele here.

evidence.snippet: H3-T45I also confers sensitivity to the DNA-damaging agent methyl methanesulfonate (MMS)
evidence.explanation: Yeast growth assays identify an additional T45I-associated stress phenotype; direct human relevance is uncertain.

evidence.snippet: four mutants – H3-T45I, -R83C, -N108S, and -A114G – cause strong His ... phenotypes, suggesting that these H3-BLBS mutants may interfere with proper nucleosome reassembly or other chromatin processes.
evidence.explanation: T45I and R83C establish H3-3A-relevant protein-level transcriptional defects in yeast. The A114G result does not establish its clinical validity.

steps/9.description: Yeast H3 mutants show separable defects: T45I and R83C permit cryptic intragenic transcription, while N108S traps FACT at gene 3-prime ends. Eight of nine newly tested mutants lack the FACT-trapping defect. Yeast native H3 expressed as the sole histone H3 source is a mechanistic surrogate, not a heterozygous human neuronal model. A114G is excluded from clinical variant inference because the study notes possible sequencing artifact.

evidence.snippet: we identified a dominant D123N mutation in h3f3a
evidence.explanation: The original allele-defining experiment excludes the previous null annotation.

evidence.snippet: A zebrafish model showed craniofacial anomalies and a defect in Foxd3-derived glia.
evidence.explanation: The model-organism result underlying this node.

steps/10.description: The zebrafish db1092 allele encodes dominant-negative D123N H3.3, rather than a null. It disrupts early cranial neural-crest specification and ectomesenchymal development, with loss of craniofacial cartilage. The 2020 study reports partial cranial-glial reductions in homozygotes and stronger deficits after added dominant-negative RNA. These peripheral neural-crest glia are not CNS radial glia or oligodendrocytes, so their loss does not establish the cause of human brain hypomyelination.

evidence.snippet: This syndrome is characterized by developmental delay/intellectual disability, craniofacial anomalies, hyper/hypotonia, and abnormal neuroimaging
evidence.explanation: States the congenital phenotype cluster this node terminates in.

evidence.snippet: Within this subgroup, 72% of individuals presented with small posterior fossa, 28% presented with dysgenesis of the corpus collosum, and 44% presented with cortical developmental abnormalities
evidence.explanation: Gives the structural findings from the detailed imaging subgroup that anchor the structural component of this node.

steps/11.description: Developmental delay, seizures and variable structural brain abnormalities define the clinical neurodevelopmental phenotype. The 2024 pooled cohort reported MRI abnormalities in 44/76 and callosal malformation/dysgenesis in 28/76. An enriched 18-person imaging series, including 11 H3-3A cases, found posterior-fossa, cortical and caudate abnormalities; those selected-subgroup rates are not population estimates.

evidence.snippet: A recent study showed that H3.3 begins to replace H3.1 and H3.2 in postnatal mouse and human brains in a time-dependent manner and displaces these canonical H3 variants almost completely in adulthood.
evidence.explanation: The founding report cites physiological histone replacement as background for a hypothesis; it did not test this as the cause of human degeneration.

steps/12.description: Age-dependent accumulation of H3.3 in postmitotic neurons is a proposed susceptibility context, not a demonstrated universal cause of BLBS1 progression. Regression is variable. The T45I mouse has motor impairment but lacks a genotype difference in the reported adult brain cell counts. G34R mice demonstrate a different, experimentally studied epigenetic route, whose generality to H3-3A patient alleles remains uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome (BRYLIB) is characterized by developmental delay / intellectual disability (typically in the severe range) and nonspecific craniofacial abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews states developmental delay or intellectual disability as a defining, typically severe feature.

evidence.snippet: Ninety-nine percent of individuals with BLBS have DD/ID (Table 1, Fig. 1D, Supplementary Table 1).
evidence.explanation: Gives the patient-level frequency underpinning the VERY_FREQUENT band.

steps/13.description: Essentially universal and typically in the severe range. Many affected individuals never achieve independent sitting, walking or speech.

evidence.snippet: Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome (BRYLIB) is characterized by developmental delay / intellectual disability (typically in the severe range) and nonspecific craniofacial abnormalities.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews names craniofacial abnormality as a defining feature and describes it as nonspecific.

evidence.snippet: In addition to growth trajectories outside of the standard range for age and sex, 92% of individuals with BLBS present with craniofacial anomalies (Table 1, Fig. 1D, Supplementary Table 1).
evidence.explanation: Gives the patient-level frequency underpinning the VERY_FREQUENT band.

evidence.snippet: Dysmorphic features are slightly more common in individuals with variants in H3-3A (95%) than H3-3B (86%)
evidence.explanation: The gene-stratified proportion supports the H3-3A description.

steps/14.description: Nonspecific facial differences were reported in 95% of the H3-3A subgroup in 2024. Population-level facial image analyses suggest patterns but do not establish a diagnostic facial appearance for every individual. Molecular testing is required.

evidence.snippet: The presentation is highly variable and can include hypotonia, epilepsy, other neurologic findings (spasticity, loss of developmental milestones, worsening gait, and/or camptocormia – forward flexion of the spine when standing that resolves when lying down), growth abnormalities (most commonly poor growth), craniosynostosis (of any suture), and ocular involvement.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews enumeration of the variable features, hypotonia among them.

evidence.snippet: Sixty-two percent of individuals presented with hypotonia whereas 12% presented with hypertonia (Table 1, Fig. 2).
evidence.explanation: Gives the patient-level frequency underpinning the FREQUENT band, and the hypertonia figure alongside it.

steps/15.description: Reduced muscle tone, common in infancy. Tone abnormality is not fixed - it may resolve with age or evolve into a mixed picture with peripheral hypertonia.

evidence.snippet: Seizures were more frequently reported in individuals harboring variants in H3-3B (59%) than those harboring variants in H3-3A (45%)
evidence.explanation: The gene-stratified observation supports the H3-3A frequency.

evidence.snippet: The presentation is highly variable and can include hypotonia, epilepsy, other neurologic findings (spasticity, loss of developmental milestones, worsening gait, and/or camptocormia – forward flexion of the spine when standing that resolves when lying down), growth abnormalities (most commonly poor growth), craniosynostosis (of any suture), and ocular involvement.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews describes the variable syndrome.

steps/16.description: Variable seizure types generally begin in infancy or childhood; 45% of the H3-3A subgroup in 2024 had seizures. Febrile, focal and generalized seizures occur, with variable treatment response.

evidence.snippet: About 25% of affected individuals show evidence of hypomyelination or delayed myelination.
evidence.explanation: The pooled estimate combines two imaging categories and cannot quantify either alone.

steps/17.description: Delayed myelination is reported in the pooled clinical literature. It should be distinguished from persistently deficient myelination using age and, when available, serial imaging. The GeneReviews estimate combines these categories and cannot establish a frequency for delayed myelination alone.

evidence.snippet: More individuals harboring variants in H3-3A (85%) had delayed or yet to be achieved independent walking when compared to individuals harboring variants in H3-3B (65%).
evidence.explanation: Gives the H3-3A-specific frequency, which is the one this entry needs.

steps/18.description: Delayed or absent independent walking, defined in the cohort as not walking by 20 months. The commonest motor milestone delay recorded. The 2024 H3-3A subgroup proportion was 85%.

evidence.snippet: About 52% of affected individuals are nonverbal, with an additional 40% experiencing speech delay.
evidence.explanation: Supports frequent severe communication impairment in the pooled clinical literature.

steps/19.description: Speech impairment is common. GeneReviews reports about 52% nonverbal and another 40% with speech delay in the combined-gene series. The 2024 table entry reporting that 50/84 spoke at least one word is an attainment measure, not a 60% speech-delay rate.

evidence.snippet: Individuals with variants in H3-3A (56%) more frequently had delayed or yet to be achieved independent sitting compared to individuals with variants in H3-3B (43%) (Fig. 2).
evidence.explanation: Gives the H3-3A-specific frequency, which is the one this entry needs.

steps/20.description: Delayed or absent independent sitting, defined in the cohort as not sitting by 12 months. The 2024 H3-3A subgroup proportion was 56%.

evidence.snippet: BLBS clinical phenotypes. ... Corpus collosum malformation/dysgenesis | 28/76 (37%)
evidence.explanation: The larger cohort supplies the frequency; the table misspelling is preserved in the exact quote.

steps/21.description: Callosal malformation or dysgenesis was reported in 28/76 of the pooled 2024 cohort. A separate selected imaging series reported 5/18, particularly affecting the splenium. These are different overlapping ascertainment groups.

evidence.snippet: Sixty-two percent of individuals presented with hypotonia whereas 12% presented with hypertonia (Table 1, Fig. 2).
evidence.explanation: Gives the patient-level frequency of hypertonia alongside that of hypotonia.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, 10% of individuals have concordant axial hypotonia and peripheral hypertonia, or dystonia, which is exclusively present in individuals with variants in the core (Fig. 2, light gray).
evidence.explanation: Records the mixed tone pattern and the fact that it occurs only with core-domain variants.

steps/22.description: Increased muscle tone. A mixed pattern of axial hypotonia with peripheral hypertonia is reported separately and occurs in about a tenth of the cohort.

evidence.snippet: Thirteen of 18 individuals (72%) presented with a small posterior fossa.
evidence.explanation: Primary imaging series; proportions are pooled and enriched for severe abnormalities.

evidence.snippet: Our cohort was biased because all individuals included in our study except for 1 had severe clinical symptoms and significant abnormalities involving the brain
evidence.explanation: The full primary study explicitly states the selection limitation.

steps/23.description: A small posterior fossa was found in 13/18 in a selected imaging series comprising 11 H3-3A and seven H3-3B cases. The severe-case enrichment prevents treating 72% as a population frequency.

evidence.snippet: Cortical developmental abnormalities were noted in 8 individuals (44%), with dysgyria and hypoplastic temporal poles being the most frequent presentation.
evidence.explanation: Primary imaging series; proportions are pooled and enriched for severe abnormalities.

steps/24.description: Cortical malformations occurred in 8/18 in the selected imaging series, including dysgyria, anterior pachygyria and simplified gyration, with bilateral temporal-lobe hypoplasia.

evidence.snippet: Chiari I malformations were seen in 4/18 (22%) of individuals imaged.
evidence.explanation: Selected imaging-subgroup finding, not a population frequency.

steps/25.description: Four of 18 in the selected imaging series had low cerebellar tonsils meeting Chiari I criteria. This is not an unselected H3-3A frequency.

evidence.snippet: About 25% of affected individuals show evidence of hypomyelination or delayed myelination.
evidence.explanation: The synthesis establishes both reported categories while leaving their individual frequencies unresolved.

steps/26.description: Hypomyelination is reported, including an H3-3A case in the 2021 series. Reduced peripheral neural-crest glia in fish does not establish its mechanism. Published pooled estimates combining delayed myelination and hypomyelination cannot quantify this finding alone.

evidence.snippet: Molecular modeling of all 37 variants demonstrated clear disruptions in interactions with DNA, other histones, and histone chaperone proteins.
evidence.explanation: The structural modelling result this node records; evidence source is COMPUTATIONAL because the claim comes from in silico modelling.

edges/1.description: Structural modeling predicts altered DNA, histone or chaperone contacts.

evidence.snippet: Three variant constructs (p.R129H, p.M121I, and p.I52N) showed significant decrease in protein expression, while one variant (p.R41C) accumulated at greater levels than wild-type control.
evidence.explanation: Transient HEK293T expression: R129H, M121I and R41C are H3-3A alleles; I52N is H3-3B and is not assigned to BLBS1.

edges/2.description: Selected H3-3A variants alter steady-state protein abundance in transfected cells.

evidence.snippet: The Co-IP assays showed that p.R129H had a significantly stronger interaction with DAXX, suggesting that this variant might affect the deposition of histone H3.3
evidence.explanation: The interaction was measured; altered deposition was inferred. HGVS p.Arg129His corresponds to mature-histone R128H.

edges/3.description: The R129H variant strengthens a measured chaperone interaction.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data suggest that the mutant histones can be incorporated into the nucleosome, cause marked local deregulation of chromatin state, and modestly alter the global control of histone modifications.
evidence.explanation: Confirms incorporation of the mutant histone and locates the deregulation at the local chromatin level.

edges/4.description: Patient-derived cells show altered histone modification patterns.

evidence.snippet: H3.3 T45I stimulates the enzymatic activities of SETD2 and NSD1
evidence.explanation: Preprint biochemical nucleosome assays support increased activity toward the recurrent H3-3A T45I substrate; this does not establish a treatment target in patients.

edges/5.description: T45I changes methyltransferase activity toward the mutant nucleosome.

evidence.snippet: four mutants – H3-T45I, -R83C, -N108S, and -A114G – cause strong His ... phenotypes, suggesting that these H3-BLBS mutants may interfere with proper nucleosome reassembly or other chromatin processes.
evidence.explanation: T45I and R83C establish H3-3A-relevant protein-level transcriptional defects in yeast. The A114G result does not establish its clinical validity.

edges/6.description: A subset of histone substitutions perturbs transcription-coupled chromatin processes in yeast.

genes/0.notes: H3-3A encodes the replication-independent histone H3.3 protein, identical to that encoded by H3-3B. Published BLBS1 alleles in the 2024 cohort are heterozygous missense changes, usually de novo. Historical population-constraint metrics support gene-level intolerance, but do not establish pathogenicity of every rare missense variant. Functional effects are heterogeneous; equal allele number is not equal protein dosage.

open_questions/1.rationale: Increased proliferation in cultured patient cells does not establish cancer predisposition. The 2025 pan-histonopathy survey reported two cancers across 192 individuals, including a pulmonary carcinoid in an H3-3B case and leukemia in an H4-related disorder. This heterogeneous, incompletely screened cross-sectional denominator cannot estimate BLBS1 incidence or lifetime risk. Tumor and constitutional sequencing and longer follow-up are needed; standardized BLBS1 surveillance is not established by these observations.

open_questions/2.rationale: The db1092 fish has a dominant-negative missense allele and peripheral neural-crest endpoints. G34R H3f3a mice demonstrate DNA-methylation and neuroinflammatory changes, but the human cases motivating that model have H3-3B variants. The 2026 L48R neural-organoid study likewise concerns H3-3B. evidence.snippet: These conditions are caused by somatic gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA, which encodes the 110-kD catalytic alpha subunit of PI3K (p110alpha). These PIK3CA mutations occur as post-zygotic events and lead to a gain of function of PI3K, with consequent constitutional activation of the downstream cascades (e.g., AKT/mTOR pathway), involved in cellular proliferation, survival and growth, as well as in vascular development in the embryonic stage.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations constitutively activate PI3K enzymatic activity.

steps/1.description: Somatic gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA (encoding the p110alpha catalytic subunit of PI3K) increase enzymatic activity, resulting in elevated PIP3 production in affected cells.

evidence.snippet: In vitro studies revealed that p.X1069Trpfs*4 mutant exhibited increased AKT phosphorylation significantly to that of the wildtype, which could be inhibited by PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitors.
evidence.explanation: In vitro functional studies confirm that CLOVES-associated PIK3CA mutations significantly increase AKT phosphorylation, demonstrating constitutive pathway activation.

evidence.snippet: These PIK3CA mutations occur as post-zygotic events and lead to a gain of function of PI3K, with consequent constitutional activation of the downstream cascades (e.g., AKT/mTOR pathway), involved in cellular proliferation, survival and growth, as well as in vascular development in the embryonic stage.
evidence.explanation: Connects mosaic PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation to abnormal cellular growth and embryonic vascular development across affected tissue compartments.

steps/2.description: Constitutive PI3K activation leads to enhanced AKT phosphorylation and downstream mTOR signaling. This results in increased cell proliferation, growth, and survival in affected tissues, driving the overgrowth phenotype.

evidence.snippet: These mutations are responsible for the clinical manifestations of the syndrome, which include low- and high-flow vascular malformations, thoracic lipomatous hyperplasia, asymmetric growth, and visceral and neurological disorders.
evidence.explanation: Review confirms that PIK3CA mutations drive the full spectrum of CLOVES vascular malformations including low- and high-flow types.

evidence.snippet: Previously intractable vascular tumours became smaller, congestive heart failure was improved, hemihypertrophy was reduced, and scoliosis was attenuated.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that vascular malformations are a key clinical feature that responds to targeted PIK3CA inhibition therapy.

steps/3.description: PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations in endothelial and lymphatic endothelial cells drive abnormal vascular morphogenesis, resulting in complex combined vascular malformations. These include slow-flow lymphatic, capillary, and venous malformations that are progressive and can cause significant morbidity through mass effect, coagulopathy, and infection risk.

evidence.snippet: Congenital lipomatous overgrowth with vascular, epidermal, and skeletal anomalies (CLOVES) is a sporadically occurring, nonhereditary disorder characterized by asymmetric somatic hypertrophy and anomalies in multiple organs.
evidence.explanation: Confirms lipomatous overgrowth as a defining feature of CLOVES syndrome.

evidence.snippet: The major deformities invariably include deposition of adipose tissue in all body regions and tissue spaces including face, scrotum, paraspinal musculature, epidural spaces, mediastinum, and pleura.
evidence.explanation: Supports diffuse adipose overgrowth including scrotal involvement.

steps/4.description: Constitutive PI3K activation in adipose precursor cells promotes excessive adipogenesis and lipomatous tissue expansion. The overgrowth is typically truncal, asymmetric, and progressive, and can involve both subcutaneous and visceral compartments.

evidence.snippet: Central nervous system (CNS) manifestations include polymicrogyria, noncontiguous abnormalities of the gray and white matter, a four-layered cortex, ventriculomegaly, hemimegalencephaly, dysgenesis of the corpus callosum, neuronal migration defects and consequent seizures, tethered spinal cord, and neural tube defects.
evidence.explanation: Directly supports a neural-development branch for CLOVES manifestations distinct from adipose lipomatous overgrowth.

steps/5.description: Mosaic PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation in neural progenitor and spinal developmental compartments produces focal brain overgrowth, cortical malformations, neural tube defects, tethered cord, ventriculomegaly, and seizures.

evidence.snippet: Previously intractable vascular tumours became smaller, congestive heart failure was improved, hemihypertrophy was reduced, and scoliosis was attenuated.

evidence.snippet: CLOVES syndrome (congenital lipomatous overgrowth, vascular malformations, epidermal naevi, scoliosis/skeletal and spinal syndrome) is a genetic disorder that results from somatic, mosaic gain-of-function mutations of the PIK3CA gene, and belongs to the spectrum of PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndromes (PROS).

evidence.snippet: These conditions are caused by somatic gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA, which encodes the 110-kD catalytic alpha subunit of PI3K (p110alpha). These PIK3CA mutations occur as post-zygotic events and lead to a gain of function of PI3K, with consequent constitutional activation of the downstream cascades (e.g., AKT/mTOR pathway), involved in cellular proliferation, survival and growth, as well as in vascular development in the embryonic stage.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations constitutively activate PI3K enzymatic activity.

edges/1.description: Elevated PIP3 recruits and activates AKT, which in turn activates mTOR signaling.

edges/2.description: Hyperactive AKT/mTOR signaling in endothelial cells drives abnormal vascular morphogenesis.

edges/3.description: Hyperactive AKT/mTOR signaling in adipose precursors promotes excessive adipogenesis and lipomatous expansion.

edges/4.description: Hyperactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in neural lineages contributes to cortical malformations, neural tube defects, tethered cord, and seizures.

edges/5.description: Mosaic pathway activation in mesenchymal and osteochondral lineages drives asymmetric limb, spinal, thoracic, hip, and craniofacial overgrowth.

edges/6.description: The same mosaic growth pathway can affect ectodermal and visceral compartments, producing cutaneous, renal, splenic, and tumor phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: We identified mutations in PIK3CA in all six individuals, and mutant allele frequencies ranged from 3% to 30% in affected tissue from multiple embryonic lineages. Interestingly, these same mutations have been identified in cancer cells, in which they increase phosphoinositide-3-kinase activity. We conclude that CLOVES is caused by postzygotic activating mutations in PIK3CA.
evidence.explanation: Landmark study identifying PIK3CA somatic mosaic mutations as the cause of CLOVES syndrome in all six patients studied, with mutant allele frequencies of 3-30% in affected tissues.

evidence.snippet: PIK3CA-related cancers and PROS share almost the same PIK3CA mutational profile, with about 80% of mutations occurring at three hotspots, E542, E545, and H1047. These hotspot mutations show the most potent effect on enzymatic activation of PI3K and consequent downstream biological responses.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the three major hotspot mutations (E542, E545, H1047) account for about 80% of PIK3CA mutations in PROS/CLOVES.

evidence.snippet: We have identified the first frameshift mutation in PIK3CA that causes CLOVES syndrome, which was confirmed to overactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway by transient transfection assays.
evidence.explanation: Expands the mutational spectrum beyond missense mutations, demonstrating that frameshift mutations affecting the PIK3CA stop codon can also cause CLOVES syndrome through PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway overactivation.

genes/0.notes: Somatic activating mutations in PIK3CA (encoding the p110alpha catalytic subunit of PI3K) are found in affected tissues. Common hotspot mutations include E542K, E545K, H1047R, H1047L, and C420R. The mutations are mosaic and often detectable only in affected tissue rather than blood. The specific mutation and its tissue distribution determine the clinical phenotype and severity.

evidence.snippet: On the basis of these results, we used BYL719 to treat nineteen patients with PROS. The drug improved the disease symptoms in all patients. Previously intractable vascular tumours became smaller, congestive heart failure was improved, hemihypertrophy was reduced, and scoliosis was attenuated. The treatment was not associated with any substantial side effects.
evidence.explanation: Landmark study demonstrating that BYL719 (alpelisib) improved symptoms in all 19 PROS patients treated, including tumor shrinkage, improved heart failure, reduced hemihypertrophy, and attenuated scoliosis.

evidence.snippet: For patients two years of age and older requiring systemic therapy, alpelisib is an option which was recently granted accelerated approval by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on April 5, 2022. Alpelisib is an inhibitor of PI3K, slowing the progression of existing lesions and preventing new lesions in patients with PROS.
evidence.explanation: Confirms FDA accelerated approval of alpelisib for PROS in patients aged 2 years and older.

evidence.snippet: we decided to discontinue Sirolimus and start targeted therapy with Alpelisib (50 mg/day). We noticed a decrease in fibroadipose overgrowth at the dorsal level, an improvement in in posture and excellent tolerability.
evidence.explanation: Case report demonstrating alpelisib efficacy in a CLOVES patient with decreased fibroadipose overgrowth and improved posture after switching from sirolimus.

treatments/0.description: Alpelisib is a selective PI3Kalpha inhibitor that has shown efficacy in reducing overgrowth and vascular malformations in patients with PROS including CLOVES syndrome. It was granted accelerated approval by the FDA on April 5, 2022 for patients with PROS aged two years and older requiring systemic therapy.

evidence.snippet: Eight patients had received previous rapamycin treatment for18 months without clinical or radiological improvement.
evidence.explanation: Eight PROS patients treated with rapamycin for 18 months showed no clinical or radiological improvement, demonstrating limited efficacy of mTOR inhibition compared to direct PI3K inhibition.

evidence.snippet: She then started treatment with Rapamycin from May 2019, without significant improvement in both vascular malformation and leg hypertrophy.
evidence.explanation: Case report demonstrating limited efficacy of rapamycin/sirolimus in a CLOVES patient, prompting switch to alpelisib.

treatments/1.description: mTOR inhibitor used to manage vascular malformations and lymphatic anomalies. May slow progression of overgrowth and reduce vascular malformation volume, though response is often limited compared to direct PI3K inhibition.

evidence.snippet: Traditional therapeutic approaches, such as sclerotherapy and surgical debulking, are often not curative in PROS patients, leading to a recrudescence of the overgrowth in the treated area.
evidence.explanation: Confirms that surgical debulking is a standard approach but often not curative with frequent recurrence.

treatments/2.description: Surgical resection of lipomatous masses and overgrown tissue. Often requires multiple procedures and recurrence is common.

evidence.snippet: Many therapeutic approaches have been attempted, including Sildenafil treatment, scleroembolization, laser therapy, and multiple debulking surgeries, but none of these were of benefit to our patient's clinical status.
evidence.explanation: Documents sclerotherapy (scleroembolization) as an attempted treatment modality in CLOVES syndrome management.

treatments/3.description: Percutaneous sclerotherapy for lymphatic and venous malformations to reduce mass effect and symptoms.

evidence.snippet: Patients with CLOVES syndrome have an increased risk of WT. Given the benefits of early detection and treatment, children with CLOVES syndrome should be considered for quarterly abdominal ultrasonography until age 7 years. Screening may be most beneficial for patients under 3 years of age.
evidence.explanation: Evidence-based screening recommendation from a cohort of 122 CLOVES patients with 3.3% Wilms tumor incidence.

treatments/4.description: Quarterly abdominal ultrasonography recommended for children with CLOVES syndrome until age 7 years, given the 3.3% incidence of Wilms tumor. Screening may be most beneficial for patients under 3 years of age.

steps/1.description: Biallelic pathogenic CNGB1 variants impair the rod channel beta subunit. Alleles include truncating, splice-site and missense changes, with effects that can differ in protein abundance, localization or gating. CNGB1a belongs to the rod CNGA1/CNGB1 channel; CNGB1b is an olfactory isoform. Not every reported variant is pathogenic and not every pathogenic allele eliminates the protein.

evidence.snippet: When expressed in a heterologous expression system the corresponding mutant full-length CNGB1a subunit was more susceptible to proteosomal degradation compared to the wild-type counterpart.
evidence.explanation: The exon-32-skipped mutant is less stable in a heterologous expression system; the full-text experiment used HEK293T cells coexpressing CNGA1. This does not establish NMD or channel trafficking in patient rods.

evidence.snippet: Since this difference in expression could be reversed by the addition of proteasome inhibitors, we concluded that the mutant protein is partially degraded by the proteasome
evidence.explanation: Proteasome inhibitor rescue supports a degradation contribution in the heterologous cell experiment.

steps/2.description: For c.3444+1G>A, exon-32 skipping replaces the terminal 170 amino acids with 68 unrelated residues. The engineered full-length mutant showed reduced abundance in HEK293T cells, reversible with proteasome inhibitors. This allele-specific instability may contribute to channel deficiency; NMD and altered targeting in patient rods were proposed rather than measured.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of CNGB1, only trace amounts of the CNGA1 subunit were found on the rod outer segment.
evidence.explanation: CNGB1-deficient mouse rods have markedly depleted outer-segment CNGA1.

evidence.snippet: In the treated region, but not the untreated, CNGA1 protein was detectable in rod outer segments
evidence.explanation: Human CNGB1 augmentation restores canine partner-subunit localization within the treated region.

steps/3.description: In CNGB1-deficient mouse rods, outer-segment CNGA1 is markedly depleted. CNGB1 augmentation restores CNGA1 abundance and outer-segment localization in mice and dogs. These findings support defective channel assembly/targeting or stability without assigning the same lesion to every human missense allele.

evidence.snippet: the vast majority of isolated rod photoreceptors in mice lacking CNGB1 (CNGB1-/-) failed to respond to light. In electroretinograms (ERGs), CNGB1-/- mice showed no rod-mediated responses.
evidence.explanation: Most isolated knockout rods were unresponsive; the population ERG lacked rod-mediated responses. Neither observation proves that every rod is silent.

evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological testing in five patients showed an absence of the rod response. Cone responses ranged from normal to severely reduced.
evidence.explanation: Human ERGs establish rod-system impairment without directly measuring channel current.

steps/4.description: Rod CNG-channel deficiency markedly reduces light responses before extensive cell loss in knockout mice and affected dogs. Residual isolated-rod responses occur, and human ERG responses range from attenuated to undetectable. Severe functional impairment is therefore distinct from physical disappearance of rods.

evidence.snippet: A feature of lack of CNG channel function in rod outer segments is the abnormal accumulation of cGMP. IHC showed that this was reversed within the treated retinal regions
evidence.explanation: In the cGMP-accumulation results section, immunohistochemistry showed reversal of abnormal cGMP staining in treated dog retina, with staining retained outside the treated regions. This is not a direct channel-current measurement.

steps/5.description: Abnormal cGMP immunoreactivity occurs in inner and outer segments of CNGB1-deficient mouse and dog photoreceptors and decreases in successfully treated retinal regions. Loss of calcium entry and its negative feedback on guanylate cyclase is proposed to explain accumulation. These observations do not establish calcium overload or directly identify the death-effector pathway.

evidence.snippet: The rods also showed a slow-progressing degeneration caused by apoptotic death and concurred by retinal gliosis.
evidence.explanation: The X26 knockout shows progressive apoptotic rod loss and associated gliosis. This does not establish the same death pathway in every human allele.

evidence.snippet: The results support previous findings of CNGB1-related RP being a slowly progressive disease with patients maintaining visual acuity.
evidence.explanation: States the natural-history cohort's overall conclusion of slow, measurable progression with maintained visual acuity.

steps/6.description: Rod photoreceptors are progressively lost following early functional impairment. Apoptotic death was demonstrated in the X26 mouse; human imaging documents structural decline without identifying an identical death program for every allele. Disease tempo differs among models and patients.

evidence.snippet: we found that GFAP was present in both untreated and late-treated retinas at 7 M
evidence.explanation: Persistent GFAP labeling after late endogenous rescue supports a sustained glial stress response in this conditional mouse model; it does not establish a causal inflammatory mediator.

steps/7.description: Reactive Müller-cell gliosis accompanies CNGB1-deficient mouse retinal degeneration. GFAP labeling decreases after effective early AAV augmentation but persists after late conditional endogenous rescue. GFAP is a stress-response readout; these experiments do not establish that gliosis alone drives ongoing cell loss.

evidence.snippet: Following late treatment, CtBP2 horseshoe structures were substantially reduced

steps/8.description: In the conditional Cngb1 mouse, late rescue leaves substantially reduced CtBP2-labeled photoreceptor ribbon structures despite surviving rods and cones. This identifies an anatomical limitation to recovery, without proving which circuit changes explain every functional deficit.

evidence.snippet: Early and mid-treatment brought the response variability back toward that of WT

evidence.snippet: Late treatment also improved the information rate of the rod-mediated RGC signaling above baseline
evidence.explanation: Late rescue retains measurable benefit without normalizing retinal output.

steps/9.description: After late conditional Cngb1 rescue, retinal ganglion cell responses have lower contrast gain and greater signal-dependent variability than after earlier rescue. Information transmission improves above untreated levels but fails to normalize and can decline over follow-up. These ex vivo mouse measurements are distinct from human visual acuity or an AAV clinical endpoint.

evidence.snippet: a gene coding for a signal transduction channel subunit expressed in rod photoreceptors and olfactory sensory neurons.

evidence.snippet: Olfactory testing revealed reduced or absent olfactory function

steps/10.description: CNGB1 encodes a signal-transduction subunit expressed in olfactory sensory neurons as well as rods. evidence.snippet: Cones were primarily unaffected and showed normal ERG responses up to 6 months, but they started to degenerate in later stages.

evidence.snippet: Taken together, this analysis of cone ERG responses provides evidence of the preservation of cone function when rod rescue is achieved by gene augmentation therapy.

steps/11.description: Cone function and structure decline after the primary rod defect. Normal early cone ERGs followed by later degeneration in X26 mice, and preservation of cone responses after rod-directed rescue in dogs, support a secondary process. The molecular intermediates are unresolved. Central vision can remain useful for years, but severity and timing vary and macular complications also affect acuity.

evidence.snippet: anosmia was diagnosed in 2 patients, hyposmia was diagnosed in 5 patients, and normosmia (borderline low) was diagnosed in 1 patient
evidence.explanation: Two of eight Sniffin’ Sticks tests met the study’s anosmia criterion. The full text additionally reports an anosmic-range T&T result in patient 9.
