evidence.snippet: TGFB3 | transforming growth factor beta 3 | hgnc:11769 | Disease-causing germline mutation(s) in
evidence.explanation: Orphanet curates TGFB3 as a disease-causing gene within the Loeys-Dietz syndrome group.

genes/0.notes: Heterozygous variants in TGFB3, encoding the transforming growth factor beta 3 ligand, cause Rienhoff syndrome (Loeys-Dietz syndrome type 5). Reported alleles fall into at least two mechanistic classes. The index de novo c.1226G>A (p.Cys409Tyr) variant lies in the last exon and destroys the cysteine knot of the mature ligand, producing a signalling-dead protein that acts as a dominant negative. A second class of variants affects codon 300 of the latency-associated peptide domain (p.Arg300Gln, p.Arg300Gly) and is proposed to increase TGF-beta signalling; these have been associated with overgrowth and tall stature rather than growth retardation. Additional variants were identified across 11 families with syndromic aortic aneurysms.

evidence.snippet: Echocardiography to monitor the status of the aortic root and ascending aorta (at least annually) and magnetic resonance angiography or computerized tomography angiography to assess the entire arterial tree
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews specifies the whole-arterial-tree surveillance regimen for Loeys-Dietz syndrome, which includes TGFB3-related LDS type 5.

treatments/0.description: Serial echocardiography of the aortic root and ascending aorta together with magnetic resonance or computed tomography angiography of the entire arterial tree. Because TGFB3-related disease involves the abdominal as well as the thoracic aorta, surveillance cannot be confined to the aortic root.

evidence.snippet: angiotensin receptor blockers, beta-adrenergic receptor blockers, or other medications are used to reduce hemodynamic stress
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews documents beta-adrenergic receptor blockade to reduce haemodynamic stress in Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

treatments/1.description: Beta-adrenergic receptor blockers reduce haemodynamic stress on the aortic wall with the aim of slowing aneurysm progression.

evidence.snippet: angiotensin receptor blockers, beta-adrenergic receptor blockers, or other medications are used to reduce hemodynamic stress
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews documents angiotensin receptor blockade for haemodynamic stress reduction in Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

evidence.snippet: At age 3 years, a 3-year trial of losartan at a dose of up to 2.0 mg/kg/day produced no change in muscle strength or mass
evidence.explanation: A prolonged losartan trial failed to improve the muscular phenotype in the index patient, arguing against TGF-beta blockade for the reduced-signalling presentation.

treatments/2.description: Angiotensin receptor blockers such as losartan are used to reduce haemodynamic stress in Loeys-Dietz syndrome. Their role in Rienhoff syndrome is uncertain and direction-dependent: a three-year trial of losartan in the index patient produced no change in muscle strength or mass, consistent with a pathophysiology of reduced rather than excess TGF-beta signalling in that allele class.

evidence.snippet: aneurysms are amenable to early and aggressive surgical intervention
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews documents early aggressive surgical repair of aneurysms in Loeys-Dietz syndrome.

treatments/3.description: Aneurysms are amenable to early and aggressive surgical repair; prophylactic intervention at appropriate thresholds prevents dissection and rupture.

evidence.snippet: The proband had physical and occupational therapy since the age 6 months, and has worn orthotic foot appliances since age 2. Although digit contractures persist, at age 9 she has very functional hands.
evidence.explanation: Documents the rehabilitative management and its functional outcome in the index patient.

treatments/4.description: Physical and occupational therapy with orthotic support addresses the contractures, hypotonia and motor delay of the muscular presentation. The index patient received both from six months of age and wore foot orthoses from age two, retaining functional hand use despite persistent digit contractures.

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Contact sports, competitive sports, and isometric exercise; agents that stimulate the cardiovascular system including routine use of decongestants or triptan medications for the management of migraine headache
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews lists the activities and agents to avoid in Loeys-Dietz syndrome, which includes TGFB3-related LDS type 5.

treatments/5.description: Individuals with Loeys-Dietz syndrome are advised to avoid contact and competitive sports and isometric exercise, and agents that stimulate the cardiovascular system including routine decongestants and triptans for migraine. This is the LDS-wide "agents/circumstances to avoid" guidance; it applies to TGFB3 carriers with demonstrated aortic involvement, and its applicability to the non-vascular presentation with normal serial imaging has not been separately studied.

evidence.snippet: Pregnancy and the postpartum period can be dangerous for women with LDS because of increased risk of aortic dissection/rupture and uterine rupture. Increased frequency of aortic imaging is recommended, both during pregnancy and in the weeks following delivery.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews documents the peripartum aortic-catastrophe and uterine-rupture risk in Loeys-Dietz syndrome and the intensified imaging schedule it warrants.

treatments/6.description: Pregnancy and the postpartum period are high-risk intervals in Loeys-Dietz syndrome, with increased risk of aortic dissection or rupture and of uterine rupture, so aortic imaging is intensified during gestation and in the weeks after delivery and medical therapy is reviewed for fetal safety.

evidence.snippet: Each child of an individual with LDS has a 50% chance of inheriting the pathogenic variant and the disorder.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews states the recurrence risk that underpins genetic counseling.

treatments/7.description: Autosomal dominant inheritance with a 50% recurrence risk for offspring, and a high de novo rate among Loeys-Dietz probands, make genetic counseling and cascade testing of at-risk relatives central to management.

evidence.snippet: we confirm a paradoxical up-regulation of both canonical and noncanonical TGF-β signaling in association with up-regulation of the expression of TGF-β ligands.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents increased aortic TGF-beta signalling in TGFB3-variant patients.

hypotheses/0.description: In patients with TGFB3-related aortic aneurysm, aortic wall tissue shows paradoxical up-regulation of canonical and non-canonical TGF-beta signalling together with increased TGF-beta ligand expression, mirroring the pattern in TGFBR1/2-, SMAD3- and TGFB2-related disease. Under this model the aortopathy arises from excess, not deficient, aortic TGF-beta signalling. This is the canonical model for the vascular presentation and is the mechanism shared with the `aortopathy_tgfbeta_dysregulation` module.

evidence.snippet: Several lines of evidence indicate the mutation is hypomorphic, suggesting that decreased TGFB signaling from a loss of TGFB3 activity is likely responsible for the clinical phenotype.
evidence.explanation: States the reduced-signalling conclusion for the index phenotype - the inference neither arm-specific sentence makes on its own. Tagged OTHER because it is the authors' synthesis pooling both functional arms rather than the report of a single experiment; the two items below cite each arm separately so that every experimental item carries one evidence_source.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that the mutant allele encodes a TGFB3 ligand that is not functional.
evidence.explanation: The cell-based arm: HEK293T-expressed, immunoprecipitated mutant ligand applied to a p3TP-Lux TGF-beta reporter generated no transcriptional signal, establishing that the p.Cys409Tyr ligand is signalling-dead.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that in the frog system the mutant TGFB3G1226A allele, when co-expressed with w-t TGFB3, has a dominant negative effect on TGF-β signaling measured by pSMAD2 and pERK1/2, but does not affect signaling by BMP2/4/7 ligands measured by pSMAD1.
evidence.explanation: The whole-organism arm, and the direct evidence for the dominant-negative claim in this hypothesis description: co-expression with wild-type TGFB3 in Xenopus embryos reduced canonical (pSMAD2) and non-canonical (pERK1/2) signalling while leaving BMP/pSMAD1 signalling intact, showing the effect is specific to the TGF-beta arm rather than general toxicity.

hypotheses/1.description: In the index patient the TGFB3 p.Cys409Tyr allele encoded a signalling-dead ligand that acted as a dominant negative, reducing canonical and non-canonical TGF-beta signalling. Under this model the phenotype (hypomyoplasia, growth retardation, distal arthrogryposis, bifid uvula, no vascular disease) follows from insufficient TGFB3 activity during mesenchymal development. Recorded as ALTERNATIVE relative to the aortopathy model not because the evidence is weaker - it is direct functional evidence - but because it is the minority explanatory model within the Loeys-Dietz framing and applies to a different allele class and tissue compartment.

evidence.snippet: increased pSMAD2 and CTGF expression was observed in the aortic media of patients with either loss‐of‐function TGFB2 or TGFB3 mutations, further confirming the paradoxical observation of increased TGF‐β signaling in vivo
evidence.explanation: Shows that loss-of-function TGFB3 alleles nonetheless raise aortic TGF-beta signalling, favouring a tissue-specific over an allele-direction resolution of the controversy.

evidence.snippet: The mutations at codon Arg300 presumably lead to increased TGF-beta signalling, suggesting that the short or tall stature seen in patients with TGFB3 mutations may result from opposing effects of mutations on TGF-beta signalling.
evidence.explanation: Proposes that opposing directions of signalling change explain the opposite growth phenotypes across TGFB3 alleles, framing the controversy.

open_questions/0.rationale: The two anchor papers for this syndrome reach opposite conclusions about the direction of the signalling defect. Rienhoff et al. showed a signalling-dead, dominant negative p.Cys409Tyr ligand that reduced pSMAD2 and pERK1/2, in a patient with normal echocardiograms through age 8 and no aortic disease. Bertoli-Avella et al. found paradoxical up-regulation of canonical and non-canonical TGF-beta signalling in aortic tissue of TGFB3-variant patients with aneurysms and dissections. A third report notes that the codon 300 (latency-associated peptide domain) variants presumably lead to increased TGF-beta signalling and are associated with tall stature, whereas the Cys409Tyr loss-of-function allele produced growth retardation - suggesting that stature itself may read out the direction of the signalling change. Whether allele class, tissue context, or the well-described paradoxical aortic response to upstream TGF-beta pathway loss reconciles these findings is unresolved, and it directly determines whether TGF-beta-directed therapy would be expected to help or harm a given patient. The strongest reconciling datum so far is that loss-of-function TGFB3 alleles are themselves associated with increased pSMAD2 and CTGF in the aortic media, which points to a tissue-compartment-specific rather than an allele-direction explanation - but that observation has not been paired with matched skeletal-muscle data from the same patients, so it does not close the question.

evidence.snippet: The principal clinical concerns for this patient have been growth retardation, weakness related to decreased muscle mass and uncertainty about her risk for vascular disease.
evidence.explanation: Names the unresolved vascular risk in the non-vascular presentation as an explicit clinical concern.

evidence.snippet: The full phenotypic spectrum and natural history of TGFB3 mutations must await other cases
evidence.explanation: The authors state explicitly that the natural history is unknown.

open_questions/1.rationale: The index patient had yearly echocardiograms from 18 months with normal aortic root dimensions at 6.5 years, and uncertainty about her vascular risk was explicitly named as a principal clinical concern. Because the same gene causes aneurysms and dissections in other families, it is not known whether childhood-normal imaging in a loss-of-function carrier predicts lifelong freedom from aortopathy or merely later onset. This gap has direct surveillance consequences for a rare disorder in which no natural-history cohort spanning both presentations exists.

evidence.snippet: Wide variation in the distribution and severity of clinical features can be seen in individuals with LDS, even among affected individuals within a family who have the same pathogenic variant.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews itself flags that feature distribution varies widely, which is why LDS-wide features cannot be assumed to apply to TGFB3 carriers.

evidence.snippet: Her skin had normal texture, tension, and wound healing.
evidence.explanation: The index patient explicitly lacked the LDS cutaneous findings, supporting the decision not to import them into this entry.

open_questions/2.rationale: The only GeneReviews chapter covering this disorder is the gene-agnostic Loeys-Dietz syndrome chapter, which pools findings across SMAD2, SMAD3, TGFB2, TGFB3, TGFBR1, TGFBR2 and IPO8. The two TGFB3-specific primary sources do not report cerebral aneurysm, craniosynostosis or the allergic/inflammatory phenotype, and the index patient is explicitly described as having skin of normal texture, tension and wound healing - a direct contrast with the LDS cutaneous triad. Arterial tortuosity, a hallmark of other LDS subtypes, is likewise absent from the TGFB3 phenotype. This entry therefore curates only features with TGFB3-specific evidence and does not import the remaining LDS-wide features, but whether their absence reflects genuine gene-specific sparing or merely the small published cohort is unresolved. It matters because gene-agnostic LDS surveillance protocols (for example cerebrovascular imaging) may be either over- or under-inclusive for TGFB3 carriers.

evidence.snippet: Mice lacking TGF-beta 3 exhibit an incompletely penetrant failure of the palatal shelves to fuse leading to cleft palate.
evidence.explanation: The supporting palatal evidence comes from complete-null mice, not from a heterozygous model matching the human genotype.

evidence.snippet: A second de novo mutation was found in TGFB3 (c.1226G>A; pC409Y).
evidence.explanation: Confirms the human disease genotype is a heterozygous missense allele, not the biallelic null modelled in mouse.

open_questions/3.rationale: The dose mismatch is the core issue: the mouse evidence for the palatal mechanism comes from biallelic nulls, whereas human Rienhoff syndrome is autosomal dominant and heterozygous. Human alleles are also mechanistically varied (cysteine-knot disruption, RKKR furin-cleavage-motif disruption, latency-associated peptide domain substitutions), so a complete null is not an obvious surrogate for any of them. The direction of effect diverges too: the mouse null is a pure loss of ligand, while human loss-of-function alleles are associated with increased pSMAD2 in the aortic media. The mouse is nonetheless the strongest available support for the palatogenesis mechanism, and the congenic-background series offers a real mechanistic parallel to human reduced penetrance - so this is a translational-validity caveat on an otherwise well-evidenced node, not an absence of evidence.

evidence.snippet: A novel SLC25A12 homozygous missense mutation, c.1058G>A; p.Arg353Gln, segregated with disease in this kindred.
evidence.explanation: Reports a specific causal variant with segregation.

evidence.snippet: Novel compound heterozygous, recessive variants in SLC25A12 were identified: c.1295C>T (p.A432V) and c.1447-2_1447-1delAG.
evidence.explanation: Reports the compound heterozygous variant pair.

steps/1.description: Two pathogenic SLC25A12 alleles are present - reported variants include the homozygous missense c.1058G>A p.Arg353Gln and the compound heterozygous pair c.1295C>T p.A432V with c.1447-2_1447-1delAG. This node records the genomic lesion only.

evidence.snippet: Recombinant mutant p.Arg353Gln AGC1 activity was reduced to 15% of wild type.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies residual carrier activity for one variant.

evidence.snippet: Functional analysis of the mutant AGC1 protein showed abolished activity.
evidence.explanation: Documents complete loss of activity for a different variant, establishing the range.

steps/2.description: The carrier's capacity to exchange mitochondrial aspartate for cytosolic glutamate across the inner mitochondrial membrane is reduced. Variant severity spans a measured range - p.Arg353Gln retains about 15% of wild-type activity while the founding variant abolished activity entirely - so the disorder is not a single all-or-nothing lesion.

evidence.snippet: as a component of the malate-aspartate shuttle, enables mitochondrial oxidation of cytosolic NADH, thought to be important in providing energy for neurons in the central nervous system
evidence.explanation: States the shuttle function that is lost.

evidence.snippet: The function of MAS in brain is essential for maintaining a NAD+/NADH ratio favorable for the oxidative metabolism of glucose
evidence.explanation: Names the redox consequence specifically.

steps/3.description: The principal neuronal NADH redox shuttle stops working, so cytosolic NADH is no longer reoxidized by transfer of reducing equivalents into mitochondria and the cytosolic NAD+/NADH ratio shifts unfavourably for glucose oxidation.

evidence.snippet: decreased baseline and maximal uncoupled respiration in neuronal cultures
evidence.explanation: Reports the respiratory deficit itself, measured in cultured AGC1-deficient neurons.

evidence.snippet: Metabolic alterations include reduced aspartate and NAA in the brain
evidence.explanation: The in vivo half of the same finding, measured in the brains of Slc25a12 loss-of-function mice, and quoted separately so each item carries a single evidence source.

evidence.snippet: As utilization of pyruvate obviates the accumulation of NADH that occurs during glucose catabolism, the ability of pyruvate to rescue these deficits is suggestive of the importance of AGC1's role in NAD+/NADH cycling
evidence.explanation: The pyruvate rescue localizes the defect to redox cycling rather than to the respiratory chain itself. Tagged in vitro because the rescue experiments this sentence interprets were done in cerebellar slice cultures and cortical neurons, not in the intact animal.

steps/4.description: Baseline and maximal uncoupled respiration fall in AGC1-deficient neurons. The critical feature is the coupling to activity: AGC1 is calcium-regulated, so the normal mechanism by which firing neurons boost their own ATP supply is exactly what is lost. Pyruvate rescues respiration, which is diagnostic of the defect being NAD+/NADH cycling rather than a primary respiratory chain lesion.

evidence.snippet: hypo myelination and a drastic drop in brain aspartate (Asp) and N-acetylaspartate (NAA)
evidence.explanation: Documents the fall in brain aspartate alongside NAA.

evidence.snippet: suggesting that impaired efflux of aspartate from neuronal mitochondria prevents normal myelin formation
evidence.explanation: Names impaired aspartate efflux as the proposed link to the myelin phenotype.

steps/5.description: Brain aspartate falls dramatically because mitochondrial aspartate cannot reach the cytosol. This is the biosynthetic arm and is measurable independently of any respiratory parameter.

evidence.snippet: in the brain, neuronal aspartate is continuously acetylated to form N-acetylaspartate (NAA)
evidence.explanation: States the biosynthetic relationship between aspartate and NAA.

evidence.snippet: abnormal myelination, fluctuating basal ganglia changes, cerebral atrophy, and reduced N-acetylaspartate (NAA)
evidence.explanation: Documents reduced NAA in affected children.

steps/6.description: N-acetylaspartate, the second most abundant metabolite in the CNS, is continuously made from aspartate in neurons. With aspartate depleted, NAA falls steeply - the finding that produces the diminished NAA peak on MR spectroscopy.

evidence.snippet: However, paradoxically, glial functions such as myelin and Glutamine (Gln) synthesis are markedly impaired in AGC1 deficiency.
evidence.explanation: States the non-cell-autonomous glial failure and flags it as paradoxical.

evidence.snippet: the aralar-KO mice model that extensively recapitulate the human disease including the astroglial failure to synthesize Gln
evidence.explanation: Confirms the astroglial defect is reproduced in the knockout mouse.

steps/7.description: Glutamine synthesis in astrocytes is markedly impaired even though AGC1 is expressed in neurons rather than astrocytes. This apparent paradox is the clearest evidence that the disorder is transcellular, and it degrades the glutamate-glutamine cycle on which neurotransmission depends.

evidence.snippet: NAA is transported to glial cells, particularly oligodendrocytes, where it is likely used for lipid and myelin synthesis
evidence.explanation: Describes the transcellular route, with the authors' own hedge on its certainty preserved.

evidence.snippet: AGC1 activity enables neuronal export of aspartate, the glial substrate necessary for proper neuronal myelination.
evidence.explanation: States the neuron-to-glia substrate relationship directly.

steps/8.description: NAA is normally transported from neurons to glial cells, particularly oligodendrocytes, where it is thought to supply acetyl groups for lipid and myelin synthesis. Less NAA means less of that supply. This is a transcellular step, distinct from both the neuronal synthesis upstream and the myelin deficit downstream.

evidence.snippet: The child had global hypomyelination in the cerebral hemispheres
evidence.explanation: Documents the global cerebral hypomyelination in the founding case.

evidence.snippet: The serial neuroimaging findings are notable for cerebral atrophy with white matter involvement, namely, early hypomyelination yet subsequent progression of myelination.
evidence.explanation: Documents that myelination progresses over time, which is the observation driving the secondary-mechanism reading.

steps/9.description: Myelination of the cerebral hemispheres is globally deficient. Longitudinal imaging in the oldest reported patient shows early hypomyelination followed by subsequent progression of myelination, a pattern the authors read as a leuko-axonopathy - white matter abnormality secondary to a primary neuronal defect - rather than a primary oligodendrocyte disease.

evidence.snippet: the dopamine (DA) mishandling in the nigrostriatal system
evidence.explanation: Names the dopaminergic phenotype reproduced in the knockout mouse.

steps/10.description: Aralar deficiency selectively affects nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons, which show altered dopamine handling in the knockout mouse. This is a circuit-specific vulnerability separate from the diffuse cortical excitability phenotype, and it is the proposed basis for the movement-disorder features.

evidence.snippet: Epilepsy and DA mishandling are a direct consequence of the metabolic defect in neurons due to AGC1/Aralar deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the epilepsy to the neuronal metabolic defect specifically, as distinct from the glial arms.

steps/11.description: Neurons become hyperexcitable despite the overall energy-deficient state. Several routes converge here - reduced activity-dependent ATP supply and disturbed glutamate-glutamine cycling among them - and the review that assembles them describes the epilepsy as a direct consequence of the neuronal metabolic defect rather than of the glial changes.

evidence.snippet: two siblings presented with profound developmental delay, congenital hypotonia, refractory epilepsy, abnormal myelination
evidence.explanation: Documents the refractory epilepsy phenotype.

steps/12.description: Seizures begin in infancy. They are pharmacoresistant in many reported children but not universally - medical control has been achieved in several - so refractoriness is a common course rather than part of the definition. The ketogenic diet, which bypasses the glycolytic NADH load the shuttle cannot handle, has produced marked benefit in reported cases.

evidence.snippet: a novel syndrome characterized by arrested psychomotor development, hypotonia, and seizures
evidence.explanation: Defines the syndrome's developmental phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Clinical presentation is characterized by severe intellectual disability, nonambulatory, nonverbal status, hypotonia, epilepsy, spastic quadriplegia, and a happy disposition.
evidence.explanation: Documents the long-term functional outcome in the oldest reported individual.

steps/13.description: Psychomotor development arrests, producing profound developmental delay and, in the oldest reported patient, severe intellectual disability with nonambulatory and nonverbal status. Three upstream routes converge here and the published cases do not apportion them.

edges/1.description: The variants reduce or abolish the transport activity of the carrier protein.

edges/2.description: AGC1 is the regulatory component of the shuttle, so losing it disables the shuttle.

edges/3.description: Aspartate can no longer be exported from mitochondria to the cytosol. This is a separate consequence from the redox one: it concerns where a metabolite ends up, not the NADH balance.

edges/4.description: Without the shuttle, glucose-supported mitochondrial respiration cannot keep pace with demand.

edges/5.description: Reduced activity-dependent energy supply is one of several converging routes to hyperexcitability; the intermediate steps are not established.

edges/6.description: Substrate limitation at complex I is proposed to underlie the selective vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons.

edges/7.description: Aspartate is the substrate from which N-acetylaspartate is made, so its depletion limits NAA synthesis.

edges/8.description: Neuronal aspartate normally serves as a nitrogen donor for astrocytic glutamate and hence glutamine; this is a non-cell-autonomous consequence.

edges/9.description: NAA is the vehicle by which neuron-derived acetyl groups reach oligodendrocytes.

edges/10.description: Reduced acetyl-group supply is the leading proposed cause of the myelin deficit, but whether the myelin failure is primary to oligodendrocytes or secondary to neuronal dysfunction is disputed.

edges/11.description: Disturbed glutamate-glutamine cycling is proposed as one contributor to the excitability phenotype.

edges/12.description: Deficient myelination contributes to the developmental phenotype alongside the bioenergetic deficit.

edges/13.description: Sustained hyperexcitability manifests as recurrent infantile-onset seizures.

edges/14.description: High early seizure burden compounds the developmental phenotype, which the metabolic and myelin arms already produce independently.

evidence.snippet: SLC25A12 encodes the neuronal aspartate-glutamate carrier 1 (AGC1) protein, an essential component of the neuronal malate/aspartate shuttle
evidence.explanation: Establishes the gene product and its function.

evidence.snippet: whereas aralar deficiency provokes predominantly neurological effects
evidence.explanation: Distinguishes this disorder from the paralogous citrin deficiency, which matters because both are aspartate-glutamate carriers; the same sentence states that citrin deficiency instead causes liver disease.

evidence.snippet: Most of these patients have homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in aralar with low or no activity of the protein as a glutamate-aspartate carrier.
evidence.explanation: Summarizes the genotype and residual-activity spectrum across reported patients.

genes/0.notes: SLC25A12 (chromosome 2q31.1) encodes AGC1, also called aralar - the neuron-specific mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier and the calcium-regulated component of the malate-aspartate shuttle. Reported pathogenic genotypes include the homozygous missense c.1058G>A p.Arg353Gln, which retains about 15% of wild-type activity, and the compound heterozygous pair c.1295C>T p.A432V with c.1447-2_1447-1delAG. The paralogue SLC25A13 encodes AGC2 (citrin), which is expressed in liver rather than brain, and its deficiency causes liver disease rather than this neurological phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Our report also provides evidence regarding beneficial effect of ketogenic diet in this rare neurometabolic epilepsy.
evidence.explanation: The authors state the ketogenic-diet benefit as a contribution of their report.

treatments/0.description: Seizure frequency abated drastically following initiation of the ketogenic diet in a reported case. The rationale is mechanistically apt: ketone bodies are metabolized without generating the cytosolic NADH load that the failed malate-aspartate shuttle cannot clear, so the diet routes around the specific defect rather than merely suppressing excitability. The response should not be read as uniform: the published clinical evidence is a small number of individual reports, and no series establishes what fraction of patients benefit or by how much.

evidence.snippet: OHB efficiently recovers aralar-KO neurons from deficits in basal-stimulated and glutamate-stimulated respiration, effects requiring βOHB entry into the neuron, and protects from glutamate excitotoxicity
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that the ketone body rescues the respiratory deficit this entry models as the bioenergetic arm.

evidence.snippet: We have investigated whether β-hydroxybutyrate (βOHB), the main ketone body (KB) produced in ketogenic diet (KD), is neuroprotective in aralar-knock-out (KO) neurons and mice
evidence.explanation: Establishes beta-hydroxybutyrate as the ketogenic-diet-derived agent under test, which is what licenses reading this preclinical result onto the diet.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: The metabolic-bypass arm. beta-hydroxybutyrate, the main ketone body produced on a ketogenic diet, recovers aralar-knockout neurons from their basal- and glutamate-stimulated respiration deficits, which is the mechanism the diet is proposed to work through in this disorder rather than by generic seizure suppression.

evidence.snippet: Patient's seizure frequency abated drastically following initiation of ketogenic diet.
evidence.explanation: Records the observed seizure response.

treatments/0/targets/1.description: Marked reduction in seizure frequency after starting the diet.

evidence.snippet: two siblings presented with profound developmental delay, congenital hypotonia, refractory epilepsy, abnormal myelination
evidence.explanation: Documents refractoriness in one reported sibling pair.

evidence.snippet: SLC25A12-related disease may be associated with successful medical seizure control
evidence.explanation: Directly qualifies the refractoriness generalization: the same paper cited elsewhere in this entry reports that medical seizure control can succeed, so refractoriness is a feature of some patients rather than of the disease.

treatments/1.description: Response is heterogeneous rather than uniformly refractory. Several reported children had pharmacoresistant seizures, but seizures were successfully treated or reduced in frequency with medication in three previously reported patients, and the oldest described individual was seizure-free off medication for several years before recurrence at about twelve. Describing this disorder as refractory without qualification overstates the published record.

evidence.snippet: A novel SLC25A12 homozygous missense mutation, c.1058G>A; p.Arg353Gln, segregated with disease in this kindred.
evidence.explanation: The segregation pattern that determines the recurrence risk.

treatments/2.description: Autosomal recessive counseling with a 25% recurrence risk per pregnancy for carrier parents.

evidence.snippet: there has been discussion in the literature as to whether this hypomyelination is primary or secondary to a neuronal defect
evidence.explanation: States the existence of the disagreement directly.

evidence.snippet: The longitudinal MRI findings are most consistent with a leukodystrophy of the leuko-axonopathy category, that is, white matter abnormalities that are most suggestive of mechanisms that result from primary neuronal defects.
evidence.explanation: The evidence for the secondary reading, and the specific classification it supports.

evidence.snippet: However, the deficits in myelin and Gln synthesis may be a consequence of neuronal affectation or a direct effect of AGC1/Aralar deficiency in glial cells. Further research is needed to clarify this question
evidence.explanation: The review states both possibilities and declines to choose, which is why this is curated as an open controversy rather than a settled chain.

open_questions/0.rationale: The mechanism curated here runs neuron to oligodendrocyte: aspartate depletion reduces NAA, NAA carries acetyl groups to oligodendrocytes, myelin lipid synthesis suffers. That chain is well motivated but the disagreement is explicit in the literature, and longitudinal imaging is what forces it. The oldest reported patient showed early hypomyelination followed by subsequent progression of myelination, which the authors read as characteristic of a leuko-axonopathy - a white matter abnormality arising from a primary neuronal defect - rather than of an oligodendrocyte disease, because a primary myelinating-cell defect would not be expected to catch up over time. The review literature is careful to leave both open, noting the glial deficits may be a consequence of neuronal affectation or a direct effect in glial cells. Two things hang on it: whether a therapy should target neuronal metabolism or oligodendrocyte substrate supply, and whether the white matter finding should be read prognostically as static or improvable.

evidence.snippet: Epilepsy and DA mishandling are a direct consequence of the metabolic defect in neurons due to AGC1/Aralar deficiency.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the epilepsy to the neuronal metabolic defect while leaving the intervening mechanism unspecified.

evidence.snippet: Herein, we discuss the role of the AGC1/Aralar-MAS pathway in neuronal functions such as Asp and NAA synthesis, lactate use, respiration on glucose, glutamate (Glu) oxidation and other neurometabolic aspects.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the candidate contributors whose relative weights are unresolved.

open_questions/1.rationale: This is the substantive puzzle of the disorder and the entry does not resolve it. Several contributors are proposed - reduced activity-dependent ATP supply, disturbed glutamate-glutamine cycling, loss of the astrocyte-neuron lactate shuttle's protective role - but none has been shown to be sufficient, and their relative weights are unknown. The paradox is not unique to AGC1 deficiency; it recurs across metabolic encephalopathies, which suggests a general principle is missing rather than a disorder-specific detail. Note that the causal edges into the hyperexcitability node are typed INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES precisely because of this: the endpoints are evidenced and the path between them is not.

evidence.snippet: Patient's seizure frequency abated drastically following initiation of ketogenic diet.
evidence.explanation: The single clinical observation on which the question rests.

evidence.snippet: OHB efficiently recovers aralar-KO neurons from deficits in basal-stimulated and glutamate-stimulated respiration, effects requiring βOHB entry into the neuron, and protects from glutamate excitotoxicity
evidence.explanation: The direct test of the proposed mechanism, which is what narrows this gap from "is the rationale even right" to "does it translate to patients". The requirement for βOHB entry into the neuron is what makes it a test of the metabolic-bypass account rather than of a generic effect.

evidence.snippet: As utilization of pyruvate obviates the accumulation of NADH that occurs during glucose catabolism, the ability of pyruvate to rescue these deficits is suggestive of the importance of AGC1's role in NAD+/NADH cycling
evidence.explanation: The parallel metabolic-bypass result in model systems, which is the basis for the proposed mechanism of the diet.

open_questions/2.rationale: The reported ketogenic-diet response is striking - seizure frequency abated drastically - and there is a clean mechanistic rationale, since ketone body oxidation does not generate the cytosolic NADH that the shuttle would normally clear. The same logic explains why pyruvate rescues respiration in the model systems, and the mechanism has since been tested directly with the diet's own active metabolite: beta-hydroxybutyrate restores basal and glutamate-stimulated respiration in aralar-KO neurons, and the rescue requires the ketone body to enter the neuron. So the mechanistic arm is no longer only an inference from biochemistry. What remains open is the translation: the clinical evidence is still individual case reports, the mechanism has not been demonstrated in patients, and no series compares early to late initiation. If the mechanistic account holds, the diet is not a generic anti-seizure measure here but a targeted metabolic bypass, which would argue for offering it at diagnosis rather than after conventional agents have failed - a materially different clinical posture from the one the current evidence supports.

evidence.snippet: the aralar-KO mice model that extensively recapitulate the human disease
evidence.explanation: States the model's claimed fidelity, which is what the caveats qualify.

evidence.snippet: Recombinant mutant p.Arg353Gln AGC1 activity was reduced to 15% of wild type.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that human genotypes retain residual activity the null does not.

evidence.snippet: the deficits in myelin and Gln synthesis may be a consequence of neuronal affectation or a direct effect of AGC1/Aralar deficiency in glial cells
evidence.explanation: The question a constitutive whole-animal knockout cannot address, since it removes the carrier from all cell types simultaneously.

open_questions/3.rationale: The knockout mouse is described as extensively recapitulating the human disease, and it is the source of most of what is curated here about the astroglial and dopaminergic arms. Two caveats limit how far that transfers. First, it is a complete null while human variants span from abolished activity to about 15% of wild type, so the model sits at the severe end of a range that patients occupy unevenly - and the p.Arg353Gln children were not obviously milder, which is itself unexplained. Second, and more consequentially for this entry, a constitutive whole-animal knockout removes aralar from every expressing cell at once, so it cannot in principle distinguish a glial defect secondary to neuronal dysfunction from a cell-autonomous one. That is exactly the distinction the hypomyelination controversy turns on, which means the model that supplies most of the mechanism is structurally unable to settle the disorder's central question.

evidence.snippet: glucose transport activity of the p.Arg176Trp and p.Ala210Val SLC45A1 variants, measured in transfected COS-7 cells, was approximately 50% (p = 0.013) and 33% (p = 0.008) lower, respectively, than that of intact SLC45A1.
evidence.explanation: Direct functional evidence that disease-associated SLC45A1 missense variants reduce glucose transport activity in a cell-based assay.

evidence.snippet: In SLC45A1 variants, the hydrogen bonds surrounding the 35th and 404th amino acid were changed, location on the cytomembrane was failed, their activity to transport glucose was also significantly decreased to contrast with SLC45A1-WT.
evidence.explanation: Independent functional replication showing mutant SLC45A1 mislocalizes and has attenuated glucose transport activity relative to wild-type.

steps/1.description: Biallelic SLC45A1 variants reduce the glucose transport activity of the encoded protein, a cerebral glucose transporter expressed in the developing and adult brain (cortex and cerebellum). Missense variants tested in transfected COS-7/COS7 cells show substantially reduced intracellular glucose transport activity relative to wild-type SLC45A1, in one case attributable to failure of the mutant protein to localize correctly to the cytomembrane.

evidence.snippet: Solute carrier family 45 member A1 (SLC45A1) is a glucose brain transporter predominantly expressed in the developing and adult brain, including the cortex and cerebellum.
evidence.explanation: Confirms SLC45A1 as a brain-expressed glucose transporter, supporting the proposed neuronal glucose transport deficit.

steps/2.description: Impaired glucose transport into neural cells is the proposed proximate mechanism linking SLC45A1 dysfunction to the neurodevelopmental phenotype, though (unlike GLUT1 deficiency) CSF glucose has not been reported as reduced in the published SLC45A1 cases.

evidence.snippet: Glucose transport across the blood brain barrier and into neural cells is critical for normal cerebral physiologic function. Dysfunction of the cerebral glucose transporter GLUT1 (encoded by SLC2A1) is known to result in epilepsy, intellectual disability (ID), and movement disorder.
evidence.explanation: The paper frames SLC45A1 as a second cerebral glucose transporter whose dysfunction is mechanistically analogous to GLUT1 deficiency, which is caused by impaired neuronal glucose uptake.

edges/2.description: Reduced SLC45A1 glucose transport activity is proposed to impair glucose uptake into neural cells, analogous to the mechanism of GLUT1 (SLC2A1) deficiency, the only other known cerebral glucose transporter disorder.

evidence.snippet: The variants segregate with the phenotype in these families, affect well-conserved amino acids, and are predicted to be damaging by in silico programs.
evidence.explanation: Establishes segregation of the SLC45A1 variants with disease in the founding families.

evidence.snippet: Through trio-based exome sequencing, the missense mutations of SLC45A1 c.103G>A (p.V35M) and c.1211T>G (p.F404C) were identified in the proband with syndromic ID.
evidence.explanation: Independent trio exome sequencing identifies compound heterozygous SLC45A1 missense variants in a proband with syndromic intellectual disability.

evidence.snippet: Pathogenic variants in SLC45A1 have been described in four patients from two unrelated families with dysmorphic features, intellectual disability, and focal epilepsy. We describe the fifth SLC45A1 patient
evidence.explanation: Confirms the small total number of reported SLC45A1 patients and adds a fifth case with compound heterozygous variants.

genes/0.notes: As of this curation (2026-07-06), only five affected individuals across three families have been reported in the literature (two consanguineous families in Srour et al. 2017, one family in Zhou et al. 2024, and one sporadic patient in Semal et al. 2025).

evidence.snippet: Meanwhile, a KD was introduced, and the child became seizure-free with cognitive improvement. After 2 years, the KD was stopped, and seizures relapsed.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents ketogenic diet efficacy (seizure freedom) and relapse on discontinuation in a genetically confirmed SLC45A1 patient.

treatments/0.description: A ketogenic diet was used in one reported patient with SLC45A1-related focal refractory epilepsy and produced seizure freedom with cognitive improvement; seizures relapsed after the diet was stopped.

evidence.snippet: Acetazolamide was introduced with seizure freedom for 10 months.
evidence.explanation: Directly documents acetazolamide efficacy after ketogenic-diet relapse in a genetically confirmed SLC45A1 patient.

treatments/1.description: Acetazolamide was introduced after ketogenic-diet relapse in one reported patient and achieved seizure freedom for 10 months.

evidence.snippet: Functional studies in vitro demonstrate that SLC10A7 mutations reduce SLC10A7 protein expression.
evidence.explanation: Establishes reduced protein expression as the shared consequence of the patient variants.

evidence.snippet: Despite similarities with the other members of the SLC10 family, SLC10A7 does not exhibit any transport activity for the typical SLC10 substrates and is then considered yet as an orphan carrier.
evidence.explanation: Supports the orphan-carrier characterization: the protein is named for a transporter family whose substrates it does not carry, so the disease mechanism cannot be read off the family name.

evidence.snippet: They show that SLC10A7 is a key Golgi transmembrane protein maintaining the tight regulation of Ca2+ homeostasis in the ER and Golgi compartments, both essential for glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: Places the protein at the Golgi and names the function whose loss starts the chain.

steps/1.description: SLC10A7 encodes a ten-transmembrane-domain protein of the SLC10 sodium/bile-acid cotransporter family which, unlike its relatives, transports none of the family's canonical substrates and remains an orphan carrier. It localizes to compartments of the secretory pathway, including the Golgi and the plasma membrane. Of the alleles actually assayed for protein level, a splice variant and the p.Leu74Pro missense reduce SLC10A7 protein expression; this is not a property of every missense allele, since p.Pro303Leu fibroblasts instead show SLC10A7 overexpression while the protein retains only partial calcium-regulatory activity. Hypomorphic rather than null function is the molecular basis of the milder end of the phenotypic spectrum. This is the disorder-specific lesion this entry substitutes for the generic Golgi trigger of the conserved CDG module.

evidence.snippet: In the present study, SLC10A7 was established as a novel negative regulator of intracellular calcium signaling that most likely acts via STIM1, Orai1 and/or SERCA2 inhibition.
evidence.explanation: Names the molecular function whose loss produces this node, and the candidate effectors.

evidence.snippet: Whereas SLC10A7 knockout HAP1 cells showed significantly increased calcium influx after thapsigargin, ionomycin and ATP/carbachol treatment, SLC10A7 overexpression reduced this calcium influx.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the direction of the effect in a null background and its reversal on overexpression.

evidence.snippet: After addition of extracellular CaCl2, SLC10A7-deficient patient fibroblasts showed a significantly increased Ca2+ influx compared with control fibroblasts.
evidence.explanation: Reproduces the calcium phenotype in cells from affected individuals rather than only in an engineered knockout line.

evidence.snippet: The present study identifies major O-glycosylation defects in both SLC10A7 KO HAP1 cells and SLC10A7-CDG patient fibroblasts and reveals an increased ER and Golgi calcium contents.
evidence.explanation: Locates the calcium abnormality inside the ER and Golgi lumen, the compartments where glycosylation occurs, and couples it to a glycosylation defect in the same cells.

steps/2.description: SLC10A7 is a negative regulator of intracellular calcium signalling, and has been proposed to be renamed RCAS on that basis. Its expression is inversely correlated with store-operated calcium entry, and it co-localizes with STIM1, Orai1 and SERCA2. Loss of function therefore raises calcium influx: SLC10A7 knockout cells show increased influx after thapsigargin, ionomycin and ATP/carbachol, and patient fibroblasts show increased Ca2+ influx after an extracellular calcium challenge. Within the secretory pathway itself the consequence is an increased ER and Golgi calcium content. Because Golgi glycosyltransferase activity and Golgi organization are calcium-dependent, this node is the rate-limiting step linking an orphan transporter to a glycosylation disease.

evidence.snippet: the proportion of heparan sulfate (HS) was significantly reduced by ~2-fold in SLC10A7-deficient patient fibroblasts compared with control fibroblasts
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the heparan sulfate deficit in cells from affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: SLC10A7 seems to play a role in Ca2+ regulation and is involved in proper glycosaminoglycan biosynthesis, especially heparan-sulfate, and N-glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: Review statement tying the calcium function to both the glycosaminoglycan and the N-glycosylation arms of this node.

evidence.snippet: We also show that the abundance of COSMC and C1GALT1 is altered in SLC10A7-CDG patient cells, as well as the subcellular Golgi localization of the Ca2+-binding Cab45 protein.
evidence.explanation: Adds the O-GalNAc arm and identifies two calcium-sensitive Golgi proteins whose behaviour changes in patient cells.

steps/3.description: Three glycosylation outputs fail together, which is why SSASKS is classified as a congenital disorder of glycosylation affecting multiple pathways rather than a single-enzyme defect. Heparan sulfate on proteoglycans is reduced roughly two-fold in patient fibroblasts and about 2.5-fold in mutant mouse cartilage, while total glycosaminoglycan content is preserved; N-glycans on plasma glycoproteins are abnormal; and O-GalNAc glycosylation is disrupted, with altered abundance of the C1GALT1 chaperone COSMC and mislocalization of the calcium-binding Golgi cargo sorter Cab45. This is the organ-agnostic substitution this entry makes against the CDG module's Golgi trigger: the module's generic disruption of Golgi glycosylation machinery is here caused by a luminal ionic lesion rather than by loss of a glycosyltransferase or of a tethering complex.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we find an abnormal N-glycoprotein electrophoretic profile in patient blood samples.
evidence.explanation: Direct human biochemical evidence of the glycoprotein abnormality.

evidence.snippet: hierarchical clustering of the plasma glycomics data was done, which indicated a subgroup of four patients that shared a unique glycomics signature of hybrid type N-glycans
evidence.explanation: Shows the glycan signature is specific enough to have been the route by which the gene was discovered, not merely a nonspecific abnormality.

steps/4.description: The Golgi lesion is readable on circulating glycoproteins. Blood spots from affected individuals show an abnormal N-glycoprotein electrophoretic profile, and the glycomics study that independently identified SLC10A7 did so by clustering a shared hybrid-type N-glycan signature out of a cohort of individuals with abnormal Golgi glycosylation. This is the biochemical readout that places SSASKS in the CDG group and the substitution this entry makes against the module's hypoglycosylation node. The module's expected edge onward to multisystem glycoprotein dysfunction is carried below, but only at the level of the disease as a whole: no study has yet linked a specific hypoglycosylated client protein to a specific SSASKS phenotype, so that edge is graded PARTIAL rather than asserted.

evidence.snippet: Cell biology studies in fibroblasts of affected individuals showed intracellular mislocalization of glycoproteins and a defect in post-Golgi transport of glycoproteins to the cell membrane.
evidence.explanation: Direct evidence of the trafficking block in patient-derived cells.

evidence.snippet: Our combined data indicate an important role for SLC10A7 in bone mineralization and transport of glycoproteins to the extracellular matrix.
evidence.explanation: Connects the trafficking defect to the extracellular matrix and to mineralization, the two downstream nodes.

steps/5.description: Beyond the composition of the glycans themselves, SLC10A7-deficient fibroblasts fail to move glycoproteins out of the secretory pathway: glycoproteins are mislocalized intracellularly and post-Golgi transport to the cell membrane is defective. Because the skeletal and dental matrices are built from secreted glycoproteins and proteoglycans, this delivery failure is the step that converts a biochemical glycosylation defect into a structural matrix defect.

evidence.snippet: We generate a Slc10a7-/- mouse model, which displays shortened long bones, growth plate disorganization and tooth enamel anomalies, recapitulating the human phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Establishes growth plate disorganization as the tissue-level lesion, in a model the authors state recapitulates the human phenotype.

evidence.snippet: The patients' phenotype consisted of amelogenesis imperfecta, skeletal dysplasia, and decreased bone mineral density compatible with osteoporosis.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the human mineralization deficit alongside the dysplasia.

evidence.snippet: alizarin red staining of calcium deposits in zebrafish morphants showed a strong reduction in bone mineralization
evidence.explanation: Independent in vivo confirmation of the mineralization arm in a second species.

steps/6.description: In the growth plate the consequence is architectural: mutant mice show shortened long bones with growth plate disorganization, and the human counterpart is disproportionate short stature with short long bones, small epiphyses and advanced carpal and tarsal ossification. Mineralization is reduced as well as growth: affected individuals have decreased bone mineral density compatible with osteoporosis, and knockdown zebrafish show a strong reduction in bone mineralization by alizarin red staining. This entry does not declare conformance to the defective_skeletal_mineralization module, because none of that module's three trigger arms (calciopenic, phosphopenic, mineralization-inhibitor excess) applies here — the lesion is failure to deliver the organic matrix, with normal calcium, phosphate and pyrophosphate handling as far as is reported.

evidence.snippet: SLC10A7-CDG patients presented skeletal dysplasia with multiple large joint dislocations, short stature and amelogenesis imperfecta likely mediated by glycosaminoglycan (GAG) defects.
evidence.explanation: States the proposed causal relation between the glycosaminoglycan defect and the joint phenotype; the authors hedge with "likely", which this node preserves.

evidence.snippet: Skeletal dysplasia with multiple dislocations are severe disorders characterized by dislocations of large joints and short stature. The majority of them have been linked to pathogenic variants in genes encoding glycosyltransferases, sulfotransferases or epimerases required for glycosaminoglycan synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Classified INDIRECT: this is background about the other members of the disease group, supporting the joint node by analogy rather than reporting anything about SLC10A7. It is why the mechanism is plausible, not evidence that it operates here.

steps/7.description: SSASKS sits nosologically among the dysplasias with multiple joint dislocations, most of which are proteoglycan-biosynthesis disorders, and the reduced heparan sulfate content of cartilage supplies the shared mechanism: proteoglycan-dependent cartilage and periarticular structures are undersupplied, and large joints dislocate. The radiographic signature — advanced carpal ossification with a monkey wrench or Swedish key appearance of the proximal femora — is shared with Desbuquois dysplasia, whose genes CANT1 and XYLT1 also act on the proteoglycan pathway.

evidence.snippet: At E18.5 labeling was observed in the inner dental epithelium of incisors and in ameloblasts and odontoblasts of molars.
evidence.explanation: Localizes expression to ameloblasts and odontoblasts specifically, which is the expression-domain argument for a cell-autonomous enamel defect.

evidence.snippet: As described earlier, all six patients were diagnosed with hypomineralized amelogenesis imperfecta.
evidence.explanation: Human evidence that the enamel lesion is present in every member of the founding cohort.

evidence.snippet: amelogenesis imperfecta seems to be a phenotypic feature specific to SLC10A7 deficiency within the group of chondrodysplasias with multiple dislocations, suggesting that amelogenesis imperfecta is not due to a defect in proteoglycan synthesis
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL because it is the authors' inference from phenotype specificity rather than a direct measurement; it is the reason this node hangs off the trafficking arm rather than the proteoglycan arm.

steps/8.description: Enamel is a secreted, protein-templated mineralized matrix, and it is the tissue in which SLC10A7 loss is most consistently expressed clinically. Slc10a7 is transcribed in the inner dental epithelium and in ameloblasts and odontoblasts during tooth development, mutant mice have tooth enamel anomalies, and every reported affected individual has amelogenesis imperfecta, typed as hypomineralized in the founding cohort and as hypoplastic/hypomineralized in the mildest case. Notably the founding study argued that the enamel phenotype is probably not explained by the proteoglycan defect alone, since amelogenesis imperfecta is what separates SSASKS from the other chondrodysplasias with multiple dislocations; the glycoprotein-trafficking arm is the more likely route.

evidence.snippet: This syndrome starts with pre- and postnatal developmental delay, and gradually presents with variable facial dysmorphisms, a short stature, amelogenesis imperfecta, and progressive skeletal dysplasia affecting the limbs, joints, hands, feet, and spine.
evidence.explanation: Describes the composite progressive endpoint and the body regions involved.

steps/9.description: The clinical endpoint is a progressive, lifelong skeletal disorder. Growth restriction is present before birth and worsens; vertebral bodies are irregular, and progressive scoliosis, hyperlordosis and kyphosis develop through childhood and drive most of the morbidity, to the point of requiring staged growth-friendly spinal instrumentation before definitive fusion at skeletal maturity.

evidence.snippet: SLC10A7 protein expression was negatively correlated with store-operated calcium entry (SOCE) via the plasma membrane.
evidence.explanation: The inverse relation between SLC10A7 protein level and calcium entry is what makes reduced protein expression the direct cause of the calcium node.

edges/1.description: Loss of the negative regulator releases the constraint it normally places on intracellular calcium.

evidence.snippet: They show that SLC10A7 is a key Golgi transmembrane protein maintaining the tight regulation of Ca2+ homeostasis in the ER and Golgi compartments, both essential for glycosylation.
evidence.explanation: Classified INDIRECT because the source asserts that both compartments' calcium regulation is essential for glycosylation without demonstrating the intervening step; the same paper states the mechanism is unknown.

edges/2.description: Luminal calcium dysregulation disturbs the calcium-dependent Golgi glycosylation machinery. This is the least directly evidenced edge in the chain and is the subject of the gap_calcium_to_glycosylation_step discussion.

evidence.snippet: Finally, we find an abnormal N-glycoprotein electrophoretic profile in patient blood samples.
evidence.explanation: The circulating readout is measured in the same affected individuals whose cells carry the Golgi defect.

edges/3.description: Defective Golgi processing is detectable on circulating glycoproteins.

evidence.snippet: SLC10A7-CDG patients presented skeletal dysplasia with multiple large joint dislocations, short stature and amelogenesis imperfecta likely mediated by glycosaminoglycan (GAG) defects.
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL because the review hedges the causal claim with "likely"; no experiment has shown the joint phenotype to follow from the glycosaminoglycan deficit.

edges/4.description: The reduced heparan sulfate content of cartilage undersupplies proteoglycan-dependent joint structures. This edge hangs off the glycosaminoglycan node rather than the trafficking node deliberately: the joint arm is the proteoglycan-mediated arm, which is exactly the arm the enamel phenotype is argued not to travel down.

evidence.snippet: Cell biology studies in fibroblasts of affected individuals showed intracellular mislocalization of glycoproteins and a defect in post-Golgi transport of glycoproteins to the cell membrane.
evidence.explanation: Both the glycosylation defect and the trafficking block are demonstrated in the same patient cells, which is the basis for placing one downstream of the other.

edges/5.description: Golgi dysfunction also blocks the onward trafficking step.

evidence.snippet: CDG are a family of rare and inherited metabolic disorders, where glycosylation abnormalities lead to multisystemic defects.
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL: this states the general CDG principle that glycosylation abnormalities produce multisystem disease, which is the basis for the edge, but it identifies no client protein or mechanism specific to SSASKS.

edges/6.description: The conserved CDG module runs from protein hypoglycosylation to multisystem glycoprotein dysfunction; in SSASKS that multisystem consequence is the skeletal and dental disease itself. The intermediates are unknown, and no individual hypoglycosylated client protein has been tied to an SSASKS phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Our combined data indicate an important role for SLC10A7 in bone mineralization and transport of glycoproteins to the extracellular matrix.
evidence.explanation: The reporting authors draw exactly this link between the trafficking function and bone mineralization.

edges/7.description: Cartilage and bone matrix cannot be assembled normally.

evidence.snippet: suggesting that amelogenesis imperfecta is not due to a defect in proteoglycan synthesis
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL: this is the authors' argument by exclusion for routing the enamel phenotype away from the proteoglycan arm, not positive evidence for the trafficking arm.

edges/8.description: The enamel organ depends on the same secretory route. This routing is an inference rather than a measurement and is the subject of the gap_enamel_route_gag_versus_trafficking discussion.

evidence.snippet: Irregular vertebral formation can lead to progressive scoliosis, hyperlordosis, or kyphoscoliosis.
evidence.explanation: States the causal step from the vertebral lesion to the clinical spinal deformity.

edges/9.description: Growth plate and vertebral involvement accumulate into the clinical dysplasia.

evidence.snippet: gradually presents with variable facial dysmorphisms, a short stature, amelogenesis imperfecta, and progressive skeletal dysplasia affecting the limbs, joints, hands, feet, and spine
evidence.explanation: Classified INDIRECT: the source groups joint and spinal involvement in one progressive process without establishing that joint laxity drives the spinal deformity.

edges/10.description: Joint laxity and dislocation contribute to the progressive deformity.

evidence.snippet: Using exome sequencing, we identify homozygous mutations in SLC10A7 in six individuals with skeletal dysplasia with multiple dislocations and amelogenesis imperfecta.
evidence.explanation: The gene-discovery study establishing SLC10A7 as causative.

evidence.snippet: In two siblings, compound heterozygous mutations were found in SLC10A7, a gene of unknown function in human.
evidence.explanation: Independent, contemporaneous identification of the gene by a glycomics-led route, and the source of the compound-heterozygous allele class.

evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous novel nonsense mutation in exon 1 of SLC10A7
evidence.explanation: Extends the allelic spectrum with a first-exon nonsense variant.

evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous missense mutation in exon 11 of SLC10A7 (NM_001300842.2: c.908C>T; p.Pro303Leu) segregating with the disease phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Source for the p.Pro303Leu allele and its segregation with disease.

evidence.snippet: The variants P303L and L210F showed significantly reduced effects on cellular calcium influx compared to the wild type but still maintained some degree of residual activity.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the functional basis for grading alleles by residual activity rather than by predicted consequence.

evidence.snippet: These findings indicate that a previously presumed complete LoF allele instead results in partial LoF, prompting a refinement of the genotype-phenotype framework for SLC10A7-related SSASKS.
evidence.explanation: The direct source for the caution against inferring allele nullity from the predicted splice consequence.

genes/0.notes: SLC10A7 is the only gene implicated in SSASKS. Reported pathogenic alleles are nonsense (p.Gly34*, p.Gln172*), splice-site (including c.472-1G>T and c.722-16A>G) and missense (p.Leu74Pro, p.Gly130Arg, p.Pro303Leu). The genotype-phenotype relation is graded by residual function rather than by variant class alone: p.Pro303Leu retains partial calcium-regulatory activity and gives the mildest reported phenotype, and a 2026 study showed that a splice allele previously presumed to be a complete null in fact leaves substantial normally spliced transcript, so allele nullity should not be inferred from the predicted consequence.

evidence.snippet: The patient received seven surgeries, which comprised rod implantation twice, lengthening four times, and final fusion once.
evidence.explanation: Documents the staged surgical protocol.

evidence.snippet: In this patient, annual check-ups and timely surgeries led to a good outcome.
evidence.explanation: Supports the outcome claim, from the same single documented course; this is one individual, not a series.

treatments/0.description: Progressive early-onset scoliosis is managed with growing-rod instrumentation, converted from single-side to dual-rod as the deformity demands, with periodic lengthening procedures and a final in-situ fusion at skeletal maturity. In the one fully documented course this comprised seven operations between roughly three and fourteen years of age and ended with a well-corrected spine and no implant complications. This is symptomatic orthopedic management; nothing is disease-modifying.

evidence.snippet: Identifying this important phenotype will improve clinical diagnosis and patient management.
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL: the source supports dental recognition as management-relevant but does not evaluate any specific restorative intervention in this disease.

treatments/1.description: Severely hypomineralized enamel requires restorative and prosthodontic management. No SSASKS-specific dental protocol has been published; care follows general amelogenesis imperfecta management, and the founding study's emphasis is that recognizing the enamel phenotype improves clinical diagnosis and patient management rather than that a particular restorative approach has been trialled.

evidence.snippet: Short stature, amelogenesis imperfecta, and skeletal dysplasia with scoliosis is a rare, autosomal recessive, skeletal disorder first described in 2018.
evidence.explanation: Supports the inheritance pattern on which the recurrence-risk counselling rests. No SSASKS-specific counselling study exists.

treatments/2.description: Autosomal recessive inheritance carries a one-in-four recurrence risk for subsequent pregnancies, which is the practically actionable point for the predominantly consanguineous families in which this disease has been reported. Cascade carrier testing and prenatal or preimplantation testing for a known familial variant follow from the molecular diagnosis.

evidence.snippet: the little finger of the right hand had displayed joint contracture since 10 years old
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL: the source establishes the progressive contracture that indicates physiotherapy, but evaluates no physiotherapy intervention. The indication is evidenced; the intervention is convention.

treatments/3.description: Joint contractures develop through childhood and joint instability limits mobility, so physiotherapy for range of motion and function is part of routine care. This is standard-of-care inference from the evidenced phenotype, not an SSASKS-specific finding: no study has evaluated physiotherapy in this disease, and none is likely at this cohort size.

evidence.snippet: mixed (one patient) and sensorineural hearing loss (one patient)
evidence.explanation: Classified PARTIAL: the source establishes the hearing impairment that indicates audiologic support, in two of six individuals, but evaluates no audiologic intervention.

treatments/4.description: Hearing impairment occurs in a subset of affected individuals; the reported findings are sensorineural loss in one individual and mixed loss in another, so audiologic assessment and hearing amplification where indicated are part of care. Assessment should not assume a purely sensorineural lesion — one later case had an As-type tympanogram indicating ossicular fixation. As with physiotherapy, the indication is evidenced and the intervention is convention: no SSASKS study reports a hearing-aid outcome. No NCIT clinical-action term for hearing-aid use exists, so this entry uses the generic supportive-care action.

evidence.snippet: Although no neurodevelopmental delay was observed to date, long-term follow-up and close attention are required.
evidence.explanation: The reporting authors' own recommendation for continued multidisciplinary follow-up.

treatments/5.description: Because involvement extends beyond the skeleton to hearing, vision and, in at least one individual, the aortic root and atrial septum, periodic audiologic, ophthalmologic and echocardiographic assessment is warranted alongside orthopedic follow-up. The one long-term report attributes its favourable outcome partly to annual review.

evidence.snippet: The mechanisms by which SLC10A7 deficiency leads to Golgi glycosylation abnormalities are unknown.
evidence.explanation: The gap stated by the authors of the most recent mechanistic study of this disease.

open_questions/0.rationale: The calcium lesion and the glycosylation lesion are each well established in patient cells, but the edge between them is inferred from the general calcium-dependence of Golgi function rather than demonstrated. The 2025 study that went furthest towards closing it opened by stating the mechanism was unknown, and its candidate mediators — altered COSMC and C1GALT1 abundance, mislocalized Cab45 — are correlates rather than a demonstrated causal chain. This matters for curation because it is the single edge on which the CDG classification of the disease rests.

evidence.snippet: suggesting that amelogenesis imperfecta is not due to a defect in proteoglycan synthesis
evidence.explanation: The inferential claim at issue, quoted with the hedge the authors used.

open_questions/1.rationale: The founding study's argument is negative and inferential: amelogenesis imperfecta appears specific to SLC10A7 deficiency within a disease group whose other members also have proteoglycan-biosynthesis defects, so proteoglycan deficiency alone is unlikely to explain it. That is a reasonable inference but not a measurement, and it is the reason this entry routes the enamel node through the trafficking arm rather than the proteoglycan arm. If wrong, the pathograph's branch structure is wrong.

evidence.snippet: Our combined data indicate an important role for SLC10A7 in bone mineralization and transport of glycoproteins to the extracellular matrix.
evidence.explanation: The reporting authors frame the mineralization deficit as a consequence of failed glycoprotein delivery to the matrix, which is the formation-side mechanism that puts this disease outside both modules' trigger arms.

open_questions/2.rationale: No, to both. defective_skeletal_mineralization is organized around three mutually exclusive trigger arms — calciopenic, phosphopenic, and mineralization-inhibitor excess — and none of them describes this disease. Calcium, phosphate and pyrophosphate handling are not reported as abnormal in SSASKS; what fails is delivery of a normally composed organic matrix, one step earlier than that module's entry points. Conforming would assert a trigger arm the literature does not support. osteoporosis_bone_resorption is declined for the opposite reason: its mechanism is increased RANKL-driven osteoclastic resorption, and no resorption abnormality has been reported here — the published defect is a formation defect, so mineral is never laid down rather than lost after the fact. This is recorded as a resolved decision rather than left as prose so that a later curator revisiting the mineralization node finds the reasoning attached to it.

evidence.snippet: However, no obvious joint dislocation was observed in Slc10a7−/− mice.
evidence.explanation: The negative result that constitutes the mismatch.

open_questions/3.rationale: The knockout has the cartilage heparan sulfate deficit that is supposed to cause the joint phenotype, yet no obvious dislocation. Either the mouse joint phenotype is present but too subtle for the assessment performed, or quadrupedal loading protects the mouse joints, or the human dislocations require something the heparan sulfate reduction does not supply. Which it is determines whether this model can be used to test interventions aimed at the joint arm at all, and the reporting authors explicitly left the question open.

evidence.snippet: Here we demonstrate that SMARD type 1 (SMARD1) results from mutations in the gene encoding immunoglobulin micro-binding protein 2 (IGHMBP2; on chromosome 11q13.2-q13.4).
evidence.explanation: Establishes biallelic IGHMBP2 mutation as the cause of SMARD1.

evidence.snippet: Like the SMN1 product, IGHMBP2 colocalizes with the RNA-processing machinery in both the cytoplasm and the nucleus.
evidence.explanation: IGHMBP2 colocalizes with the RNA-processing machinery, supporting its role in mRNA processing.

evidence.snippet: Biochemical characterization has determined that IGHMBP2 is an ATP‐dependent 5’→3’ DNA/RNA helicase.
evidence.explanation: Defines the ATP-dependent 5'->3' DNA/RNA helicase activity of IGHMBP2.

evidence.snippet: Most SMARD1‐causing missense mutations have been found in the helicase domain
evidence.explanation: Locates the SMARD1-causing mutations in the helicase domain, supporting helicase deficiency as the molecular lesion.

steps/1.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in IGHMBP2 reduce or abolish the function of an ATP-dependent 5'->3' DNA/RNA helicase of superfamily 1 (UPF1-like) that associates with ribosomes in the cytoplasm and colocalizes with the RNA-processing machinery. The deficiency is thought to impair pre-mRNA processing and ribosomal translation/biogenesis required for motor neuron maintenance and integrity. Most SMARD1-causing missense mutations cluster in the helicase domain.

evidence.snippet: The initial symptoms of patients with SMARD1 are respiratory distress and distal muscle weakness manifesting in the infantile period due to progressive degeneration of α-motor neurons.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the infantile respiratory distress and distal weakness to progressive alpha motor neuron degeneration.

evidence.snippet: SMARD1 patients typically present with phrenic nerve palsy between the ages of six weeks and six months, and motor neuron degeneration primarily affects the distal muscles, particularly those of the lower extremities.
evidence.explanation: Documents the distal-predominant pattern of motor neuron degeneration with early phrenic involvement.

evidence.snippet: indicate that IGHMBP2 and SMN share common functions important for motor neuron maintenance and integrity in mammals
evidence.explanation: Links IGHMBP2 function to motor neuron maintenance and integrity.

steps/2.description: Progressive degeneration of spinal anterior-horn lower (alpha) motor neurons, beginning before clinical symptom onset, with a characteristic distal-predominant and diaphragmatic/phrenic predilection. Motor neuron loss preferentially affects the distal muscles, particularly the lower extremities, while phrenic motor output to the diaphragm fails early.

evidence.snippet: Respiratory distress is usually the presenting clinical symptom and occurs between 6 weeks and 6 months of age as a consequence of the development of neurogenic diaphragmatic palsy.
evidence.explanation: Links neurogenic diaphragmatic palsy to the presenting respiratory distress of SMARD1.

evidence.snippet: the characteristic eventration (the abnormal elevation) of the right or, less frequently, both hemidiaphragms, which is considered a highly suggestive sign of SMARD1
evidence.explanation: Diaphragmatic eventration on chest X-ray is a hallmark radiographic sign of SMARD1.

evidence.snippet: it presents with respiratory failure due to diaphragmatic paralysis, progressive muscle weakness starting in the distal parts of the limbs, dysphagia, and damage to sensory and autonomic nerves
evidence.explanation: Describes respiratory failure from diaphragmatic paralysis with distal-onset weakness and sensory/autonomic involvement.

steps/3.description: Degeneration of the phrenic nerve and its motor neurons causes neurogenic diaphragmatic palsy, manifest radiographically as eventration (abnormal elevation) of the right or both hemidiaphragms—a highly suggestive sign of SMARD1—and clinically as respiratory distress and failure requiring mechanical ventilation between 6 weeks and 6 months of age. Unlike SMN1-related SMA, the thorax is normally shaped because the defect mainly involves the diaphragm.

evidence.snippet: The degeneration of the phrenic nerve is accompanied by the progressive wasting of the distal muscles of the limbs; the lower limbs are affected earlier than the upper limbs, and the proximal muscles become affected along with the progression of the disease.
evidence.explanation: Documents the distal-onset, lower-limb-predominant, progressive denervation pattern.

evidence.snippet: progressive autonomic nervous system dysfunction also develops in association with the progressive worsening of motor functions in affected children
evidence.explanation: Establishes progressive autonomic involvement accompanying motor decline.

steps/4.description: Distal denervation from lower motor neuron loss produces progressive wasting of the distal limb muscles—lower limbs affected earlier than upper—extending proximally with disease progression, with loss of deep tendon reflexes (areflexia), foot deformities, and progressive autonomic and sensory involvement.

evidence.snippet: Most children with SMARD1 do not survive beyond the first year of life due to progressive respiratory failure.
evidence.explanation: Respiratory failure is the leading cause of early mortality in SMARD1.

steps/5.description: Infantile respiratory distress progressing to respiratory failure from neurogenic diaphragmatic palsy, typically requiring mechanical ventilation between 6 weeks and 6 months of age; the leading cause of early mortality.
